deduped_items.summary: Assaltante é atingido por pedrada durante crime e desmaia Duas pessoas impediram um assalto no último sábado (26) após jogarem pedras contra dois suspeitos que abordaram um casal no bairro São José, em Juazeiro do Norte, no Ceará. Câmeras de segurança registraram toda a ação. Na gravação, um dos suspeitos, armado com um facão, se aproxima de um estabelecimento comercial e anuncia o assalto. Poucos segundos depois, um casal chega ao local em uma moto e também é abordado pelo homem. ✅ Clique e sig
deduped_items.body_text:
Duas pessoas impediram um assalto no último sábado (26) após jogarem pedras contra dois suspeitos que abordaram um casal no bairro São José, em Juazeiro do Norte, no Ceará. Câmeras de segurança registraram toda a ação.
Na gravação, um dos suspeitos, armado com um facão, se aproxima de um estabelecimento comercial e anuncia o assalto. Poucos segundos depois, um casal chega ao local em uma moto e também é abordado pelo homem.
Em seguida, o comparsa se aproxima e participa da ação. Conforme apuração da TV Verdes Mares, as vítimas foram ameaçadas para entregar os celulares e a motocicleta.
Ao perceberem o assalto, populares que estavam nas proximidades reagiram e começaram a jogar pedras contra os suspeitos. Um deles, que já estava em cima da motocicleta, foi atingido na cabeça e caiu do veículo. O outro conseguiu fugir do local.
Conforme a Secretaria da Segurança Pública, o homem atingido pela pedrada já responde pelos crimes de roubo e furto.
Dupla foi capturada pela Polícia. — Foto: Reprodução
Policiais capturaram um dos suspeitos caído no chão e com lesões. Ele foi levado para o Hospital Regional do Cariri para receber atendimento médico.
O outro suspeito, que havia fugido levando os celulares, foi localizado posteriormente por populares. Ele também apresentava lesões e foi encaminhado para uma Unidade de Pronto Atendimento (UPA).
Durante as diligências, um dos celulares roubados foi recuperado. Após receberem atendimento médico, os dois suspeitos foram apresentados e ficaram detidos. Um deles permaneceu sob escolta policial no Hospital Regional do Cariri.
Criminoso é atingido por pedrada enquanto tentava levar moto de assalto no Ceará — Foto: Reprodução

deduped_items.summary: Homem morre e adolescente fica ferido após serem baleados na Grande São Luís Um homem morreu e um adolescente ficou ferido após serem baleados na madrugada desta terça-feira (29), no bairro Maiobão, em Paço do Lumiar, na Região Metropolitana de São Luís. Segundo a Polícia Civil do Maranhão (PC-MA), os dois estavam em uma motocicleta quando foram abordados por ocupantes de um veículo, que efetuaram disparos de arma de fogo contra eles. 📲 Clique aqui e se inscreva no canal do g1 Maranhão no WhatsA
deduped_items.body_text:
Um homem morreu e um adolescente ficou ferido após serem baleados na madrugada desta terça-feira (29), no bairro Maiobão, em Paço do Lumiar, na Região Metropolitana de São Luís.
Segundo a Polícia Civil do Maranhão (PC-MA), os dois estavam em uma motocicleta quando foram abordados por ocupantes de um veículo, que efetuaram disparos de arma de fogo contra eles.
A vítima morta foi identificada inicialmente apenas pelo nome de Kauan. A segunda foi um adolescente de 17 anos, que apresentava ferimentos na perna e foi socorrido e encaminhado ao Hospital da Cidade Dr. Jackson Lago (Socorrão II), em São Luís.
Homem morre e adolescente fica ferido após serem baleados no Maiobão, em Paço do Lumiar — Foto: Divulgação/Redes sociais
O crime aconteceu por volta das 4h37, na Avenida Quatro, em frente ao Convento das Freiras. A Polícia Militar foi acionada após denúncias de que duas pessoas haviam sido baleadas e estavam caídas no local.
Ao chegarem ao endereço, os policiais encontraram as duas vítimas próximas a uma motocicleta. O Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) foi chamado e confirmou a morte de uma delas ainda no local.
Durante a ocorrência, os policiais localizaram um simulacro de arma de fogo, do tipo pistola, nas proximidades das vítimas. O objeto foi apreendido e será analisado no decorrer das investigações. O adolescente sobrevivente negou ser o proprietário do simulacro.
A motocicleta encontrada no local, uma Honda CG 160 Fan, de cor preta, placa PTK1B03, foi consultada pela polícia e não apresentava registro de roubo ou furto.
A Superintendência Estadual de Homicídios e de Proteção à Pessoa (SHPP) instaurou um inquérito para investigar o caso, que é tratado como homicídio e tentativa de homicídio.
As investigações seguem em andamento para esclarecer a motivação do crime e identificar os autores dos disparos.

deduped_items.body_text:
Safira e Amora (da esquerda para a direita), cadelas do Canil do Corpo de Bombeiros de Roraima. — Foto: Neto Figueredo e Ascom/CBMRR/Divulgação
Usar a agilidade e os sentido aguçados para salvar vidas é uma das funções das cadelas Amora e Safira, do Canil da Companhia de Busca e Salvamento do Corpo de Bombeiros de Roraima. As duas foram certificadas em um processo nacional para atuar em buscas e resgates de pessoas vivas em áreas urbanas.
O processo ocorreu entre os dias 14 e 21 de setembro, no Rio de Janeiro (RJ), durante a etapa Sudeste da certificação nacional. Ele é realizado pelo Comitê Nacional de Busca, Resgate e Salvamento com Cães (Conabresc).
🔎 A avaliação define quais duplas, formadas por um cão e um bombeiro militar, estão aptas a atuar em missões de busca, resgate e salvamento. Entre os aspectos verificados estão obediência, capacidade de busca, faro e agilidade.
O processo é dividido em fases como a de inspeção sanitária, testes de habilidades fundamentais e a busca. O objetivo é verificar se ambos estão preparados para atuar em ocorrências reais.
Amora, da raça rastreador brasileiro, e Safira, da raça pastor belga malinois, foram avaliadas com os condutores, os sargentos Fausto Santos Bandeira da Silva e Jocimar Nascimento Alves Pereira. Amora passou pelo processo de recertificação, enquanto Safira recebeu o primeiro certificado nacional.
Amora e Safira, cadelas do Corpo de Bombeiros de Roraima, e os condutores sargentos Fausto Bandeira e Jocimar Nascimento. — Foto: Neto Figueredo e Ascom/CBMRR/Divulgação
LEIA TAMBÉM:
'Trabalho longo'
Condutor da Amora, Fausto Bandeira explicou que a preparação para uma certificação pode levar cerca de um ano e meio. Aos quatro anos, a cadela já participou de três processos de certificação.
A primeira certificação da cadela ocorreu em 2024, em João Pessoa (PB), na modalidade Urbano Vivo. Em 2025, em Fortaleza (CE), Amora obteve certificação na modalidade Restos Mortais Urbano.
“É um trabalho longo. A gente leva, em média, um ano e meio preparando o cão para poder participar da certificação. A Amora já está com quatro anos e, nesse período, tivemos a oportunidade de participar de três certificações", disse Bandeira. 
Amora passou pelo processo de recertificação e chegou à terceira certificação. — Foto: Neto Figueredo e Ascom/CBMRR/Divulgação
O processo de preparação de Safira começou quando ela ainda era filhote. Atualmente, a pastor belga tem dois anos.
O condutor Jocimar Nascientou ressaltou que o treinamento envolve não apenas o desenvolvimento da capacidade de busca, mas também a convivência dos animais entre si e com as pessoas.
“O trabalho é conjunto. Os cães precisam ser associados, não podem ser agressivos com outros cães nem com os seres humanos. Então, um ajuda o outro, e o treinamento acaba sendo realizado em conjunto”, explicou. 
Além das cadelas certificadas, o Canil da Companhia de Busca e Salvamento mantém outros cães em treinamento. A preparação inclui diferentes modalidades de busca e forma novas duplas de cães e condutores para atuar em ocorrências em Roraima e, quando necessário, em apoio a outros estados.
Processo de preparação de Safira durou cerca de dois anos. — Foto: Neto Figueredo e Ascom/CBMRR/Divulgação

Duas pessoas impediram um assalto no último sábado (26) após jogarem pedras contra dois suspeitos que abordaram um casal no bairro São José, em Juazeiro do Norte, no Ceará. Câmeras de segurança registraram toda a ação.
Na gravação, um dos suspeitos, armado com um facão, se aproxima de um estabelecimento comercial e anuncia o assalto. Poucos segundos depois, um casal chega ao local em uma moto e também é abordado pelo homem.
Em seguida, o comparsa se aproxima e participa da ação. Conforme apuração da TV Verdes Mares, as vítimas foram ameaçadas para entregar os celulares e a motocicleta.

Conforme a Secretaria da Segurança Pública, o homem atingido pela pedrada já responde pelos crimes de roubo e furto.

deduped_items.title: Brasil seguir nacionalismo de Trump seria ruim para o mundo, diz Piketty à BBC News Brasil
deduped_items.summary: Para economista francês, 'estamos em um período repleto de distopias. Os tecnobilionários, os tecnonacionalistas estão elaborando visões malucas sobre o futuro'. Mesmo assim, ele se diz otimista, e que 'a longo prazo, as forças democráticas e as lutas sociais estarão prontas para fazer do mundo um lugar mais igualitário e próspero'.
deduped_items.body_text:
Veja as estimativas de intenção de voto no Agregador de Pesquisas da BBC News Brasil
Brasil seguir nacionalismo de Trump seria ruim para o mundo, diz Piketty à BBC News Brasil
  - Author, Vinícius Mendes
  - Role, Da BBC News Brasil em São Paulo
- Published
- Tempo de leitura: 13 min
Cinco anos atrás, uma percepção do economista francês Thomas Piketty, 55 anos, rodou o planeta. Ela defendia que o mundo estava em condições parecidas às que desaguaram na Revolução Francesa, no fim do século 18: uma desigualdade extrema em que elites riquíssimas (a nobreza daquela França) viviam às custas de uma multidão de pessoas em situações precárias.
Era mais um alerta do que uma comparação, porque, sempre que isso aconteceu na história, o resultado foi uma grave crise política capaz de mudar o rumo das coisas.
"Em muitos sentidos, [a situação] piorou" nesse intervalo de meia década, sentencia ele agora à BBC News Brasil.
"Estamos em um período repleto de distopias. Os tecnobilionários, os tecnonacionalistas estão elaborando visões malucas sobre o futuro", diz ele, alertando para "uma visão trumpista do futuro que não está funcionando, que não resolve problemas de desenvolvimento, de meio ambiente, que precisamos resolver".
Piketty retornou à cena global em junho com um conjunto audacioso de propostas reunidas no Relatório de Justiça Global. É o resultado do esforço conjunto de uma equipe liderada por ele, no World Inequality Lab, da Paris School of Economics, na capital francesa, que se debruçou sobre dados sociais e econômicos de vários países ao longo dos últimos anos.
No total, cerca de 50 pessoas trabalharam no estudo, que elaborou propostas como criar uma moeda única internacional, gerida pela Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU), em substituição ao dólar, e impulsionar políticas globais que nivelem a renda per capita global em 5 mil euros (cerca de R$ 29 mil, na cotação do final de setembro) até 2100.
O relatório também propõe que, até lá, o total de horas de trabalho, na média internacional, cairia para menos da metade, com um deslocamento das funções ligadas à produção de alimentos para os setores de educação e saúde.
Além disso, há propostas historicamente ligadas às pesquisas de Piketty — que se tornou famoso, nos anos 2010, com seu O capital no século XXI (Intrínseca, 2013) – como a criação de um imposto global sobre a riqueza e, especialmente, sobre fortunas dos bilionários.
E aí que, para ele, o Brasil exerce um papel central. Em 2024, durante a reunião do G20, no Rio de Janeiro, o país conseguiu incluir uma menção inédita à importância de tributar os super-ricos no comunicado final da Cúpula, apesar da dura resistência argentina.
Nos fóruns que se seguiram, a diplomacia brasileira seguiu reforçando o projeto, como nas rodadas de negociação, no âmbito da ONU, por um sistema tributário internacional. A próxima reunião do grupo será realizada entre novembro e dezembro, no Quênia.
"Será muito triste para o próprio país tanto quanto para o mundo se o Brasil seguir na direção desse nacionalismo trumpista em algumas semanas [nas eleições]. Precisamos do Brasil contribuindo para reconstruir o sistema monetário, econômico internacional em um sentido mais inclusivo, igualitário, democrático e consciente sobre o clima", diz.
A seguir, trechos da entrevista que Thomas Piketty concedeu à BBC News Brasil alguns dias antes do primeiro turno da eleição presidencial brasileira.
BBC News Brasil - Como acomodar pretensões globais tão robustas em um mundo atravessado por conflitos e por Estados nacionais mais voltados aos seus interesses particulares?
Thomas Piketty - Estamos em um período repleto de distopias. Os tecnobilionários, os tecnonacionalistas estão elaborando visões malucas sobre o futuro, como instalar data centers em todos os lugares possíveis — no planeta Terra ou em Marte — e estão fazendo guerras para extrair ainda mais combustíveis fósseis pelo mundo. É uma visão trumpista do futuro que não está funcionando, que não resolve proble

Mesmo assim, ele se diz otimista, e que 'a longo prazo, as forças democráticas e as lutas sociais estarão prontas para fazer do mundo um lugar mais igualitário e próspero'.
deduped_items.body_text:
Veja as estimativas de intenção de voto no Agregador de Pesquisas da BBC News Brasil
Brasil seguir nacionalismo de Trump seria ruim para o mundo, diz Piketty à BBC News Brasil
  - Author, Vinícius Mendes
  - Role, Da BBC News Brasil em São Paulo
- Published
- Tempo de leitura: 13 min
Cinco anos atrás, uma percepção do economista francês Thomas Piketty, 55 anos, rodou o planeta. Ela defendia que o mundo estava em condições parecidas às que desaguaram na Revolução Francesa, no fim do século 18: uma desigualdade extrema em que elites riquíssimas (a nobreza daquela França) viviam às custas de uma multidão de pessoas em situações precárias.
Era mais um alerta do que uma comparação, porque, sempre que isso aconteceu na história, o resultado foi uma grave crise política capaz de mudar o rumo das coisas.
"Em muitos sentidos, [a situação] piorou" nesse intervalo de meia década, sentencia ele agora à BBC News Brasil.
"Estamos em um período repleto de distopias. Os tecnobilionários, os tecnonacionalistas estão elaborando visões malucas sobre o futuro", diz ele, alertando para "uma visão trumpista do futuro que não está funcionando, que não resolve problemas de desenvolvimento, de meio ambiente, que precisamos resolver".
Piketty retornou à cena global em junho com um conjunto audacioso de propostas reunidas no Relatório de Justiça Global. É o resultado do esforço conjunto de uma equipe liderada por ele, no World Inequality Lab, da Paris School of Economics, na capital francesa, que se debruçou sobre dados sociais e econômicos de vários países ao longo dos últimos anos.
No total, cerca de 50 pessoas trabalharam no estudo, que elaborou propostas como criar uma moeda única internacional, gerida pela Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU), em substituição ao dólar, e impulsionar políticas globais que nivelem a renda per capita global em 5 mil euros (cerca de R$ 29 mil, na cotação do final de setembro) até 2100.
O relatório também propõe que, até lá, o total de horas de trabalho, na média internacional, cairia para menos da metade, com um deslocamento das funções ligadas à produção de alimentos para os setores de educação e saúde.
Além disso, há propostas historicamente ligadas às pesquisas de Piketty — que se tornou famoso, nos anos 2010, com seu O capital no século XXI (Intrínseca, 2013) – como a criação de um imposto global sobre a riqueza e, especialmente, sobre fortunas dos bilionários.
E aí que, para ele, o Brasil exerce um papel central. Em 2024, durante a reunião do G20, no Rio de Janeiro, o país conseguiu incluir uma menção inédita à importância de tributar os super-ricos no comunicado final da Cúpula, apesar da dura resistência argentina.
Nos fóruns que se seguiram, a diplomacia brasileira seguiu reforçando o projeto, como nas rodadas de negociação, no âmbito da ONU, por um sistema tributário internacional. A próxima reunião do grupo será realizada entre novembro e dezembro, no Quênia.
"Será muito triste para o próprio país tanto quanto para o mundo se o Brasil seguir na direção desse nacionalismo trumpista em algumas semanas [nas eleições]. Precisamos do Brasil contribuindo para reconstruir o sistema monetário, econômico internacional em um sentido mais inclusivo, igualitário, democrático e consciente sobre o clima", diz.
A seguir, trechos da entrevista que Thomas Piketty concedeu à BBC News Brasil alguns dias antes do primeiro turno da eleição presidencial brasileira.
BBC News Brasil - Como acomodar pretensões globais tão robustas em um mundo atravessado por conflitos e por Estados nacionais mais voltados aos seus interesses particulares?
Thomas Piketty - Estamos em um período repleto de distopias. Os tecnobilionários, os tecnonacionalistas estão elaborando visões malucas sobre o futuro, como instalar data centers em todos os lugares possíveis — no planeta Terra ou em Marte — e estão fazendo guerras para extrair ainda mais combustíveis fósseis pelo mundo. É uma visão trumpista do futuro que não está funcionando, que não resolve proble

  - Author, Vinícius Mendes
  - Role, Da BBC News Brasil em São Paulo
- Published
- Tempo de leitura: 13 min
Cinco anos atrás, uma percepção do economista francês Thomas Piketty, 55 anos, rodou o planeta. Ela defendia que o mundo estava em condições parecidas às que desaguaram na Revolução Francesa, no fim do século 18: uma desigualdade extrema em que elites riquíssimas (a nobreza daquela França) viviam às custas de uma multidão de pessoas em situações precárias.
Era mais um alerta do que uma comparação, porque, sempre que isso aconteceu na história, o resultado foi uma grave crise política capaz de mudar o rumo das coisas.
"Em muitos sentidos, [a situação] piorou" nesse intervalo de meia década, sentencia ele agora à BBC News Brasil.
"Estamos em um período repleto de distopias. Os tecnobilionários, os tecnonacionalistas estão elaborando visões malucas sobre o futuro", diz ele, alertando para "uma visão trumpista do futuro que não está funcionando, que não resolve problemas de desenvolvimento, de meio ambiente, que precisamos resolver".

deduped_items.title: Tinubu writes Senate, seeks approval to establish National Research Development Fund
deduped_items.summary: By Henry Umoru ABUJA- PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has written the Senate, seeking for the approval to establish the National Research and Development Fund. The letter by the President was read yesterday by the President of the Senate, Sen. Godswill Akpabio, upon the resumption of plenary following a nine-week recess. According to the President, the National […] The post Tinubu writes Senate, seeks approval to establish National Research Development Fund appeared first on Vanguard News.
deduped_items.body_text:
File image of President Tinubu.
By Henry Umoru
ABUJA- PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has written the Senate, seeking for the approval to establish the National Research and Development Fund.
The letter by the President was read yesterday by the President of the Senate, Sen. Godswill Akpabio, upon the resumption of plenary following a nine-week recess.
According to the President, the National Research and Development Fund (Establishment) Bill, 2026 is to consolidate research financing, ensure more efficient utilization of resources, and to consolidate the fragmented Research and Development Funds across Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) into the National Research and Development Fund to serve as a central mechanism through which research agencies and academic institutions can access funding.
The letter read, “I am pleased to transmit to the Senate, for consideration, the National Research and Development Fund (Establishment) Bill, 2026.
“The Bill is prepared in a bid to consolidate research financing, ensure more efficient utilization of resources, and to consolidate the fragmented Research and Development Funds across Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs) into the National Research and Development Fund to serve as a central mechanism through which research agencies and academic institutions can access funding.
“The establishment of the National Research and Development Fund will serve as a competitive central funding mechanism. It seeks to foster strategic collaboration among research agencies, academia and the private sector. It will catalyze groundbreaking innovations, streamline resource allocation according to strategic national priorities, ensure strict transparency in funding decisions through evaluation criteria, and drive the commercialization of home-grown technology to reduce foreign technological dependency.
“Going further, the Bill establishes the National Research and Development Fund as an Agency under the supervision of the Federal Ministry of Innovation, Science and Technology, with direct funding from the Nigerian Content Development Fund.
“It is pertinent to note that with the current proliferation of research institutions and agencies operating within the research and development commercialization landscape, each agency operates with a separate mandate and budgetary allocations. The Bill therefore seeks to enable effective management of the limited financial resources available to these institutes and research agencies for the efficient development of Science, Technology and Innovation in Nigeria.
“The Bill has been thoroughly reviewed and vetted by relevant key stakeholders, including the Ministries of Education and Innovation, Science and Technology, as well as the Ministry of Justice, to ensure that the legislative structure aligns seamlessly with national education objectives and scientific innovation priorities, while ensuring legal precision, institutional harmony and statutory clarity.
“In consequence of the above, the National Research and Development Fund (Establishment) Bill, 2026 is hereby forwarded to the Senate for legislative action by the National Assembly.
“While it is my hope that the Senate will consider the Bill and its passage into law expeditiously, please accept, Distinguished Senate President, Distinguished Senators, the assurances of my highest consideration.”
The bill was referred to the Senate Committee on Rules and Business for further legislative consideration.

deduped_items.body_text:
ISLAMABAD: Opposition alliance Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) on Tuesday invited the PPP, a key ally of the ruling PML-N in the Centre, to attend multiparty conference that is being planned by the opposition.
For its part, the PPP said it “welcomes the move” and would forward the invitation to the party’s chairperson, Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari. The TTAP would then be informed of his stance.
The development was confirmed in separate but similar statements by the two sides.
The opposition had first announced its intention to hold a multiparty moot on Sept 11, with the PTI leading the initiative. PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan had outlined plans to hold the conference, saying that “the current law and order situation, the economy, inflation, lawlessness, and the creation of new provinces issue” called for such measures.
His statement to the media came after a meeting with Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) leaders, who have agreed to attend the opposition’s moot.
A delegation of the TTAP, led by Barrister Gohar, called on PPP Secretary General Nayyar Hussain Bukhari at the party’s Central Secretariat in Islamabad and formally invited his party to the moot as well, statements by the two sides said.
The delegation also included Leader of Opposition in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, Senator Zeeshan Akhunzada and TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Yousafzai.
The TTAP delegation briefed Bukhari on the objectives and purpose of the planned multiparty conference, the statements said.
They also discussed the political situation in the country, supremacy of the Constitution, strengthening of democratic institutions, contacts between political parties and other matters.
The statements quoted Bukhari as saying that the PPP considered “engagement and consultation with political parties on constitutional and democratic matters important”.
Speaking to Dawn after the meeting, TTAP spokesperson Yousafzai said the multiparty conference would be held after PTI’s protest, which is scheduled for Oct 4 to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan.
“We have started meeting with the representatives of political parties so that the date and venue for the moot is finalised,” he said, adding that since the PPP had taken a clear stance over the creation of new provinces, the opposition had decided to invite it as well.
In the recent past, the proposal for the creation of new administrative units was first floated by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi in July. The proposition drew strong reactions from government ministers, while the country’s leading lawyers’ bodies adopted divergent positions.
The PPP, which rules Sindh, has strongly opposed any division of the province and maintains that any decision to create new provinces must be taken through the constitutional and parliamentary process and with political consensus.
Meanwhile, the relationship between the PPP and the PML-N had also been strained lately during acrimonious election campaigns in Azad Jammu and Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan.
The TTAP also plans invite other parties to the opposition’s moot.
Yousafzai said Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam (JUI), Awami National Party (ANP) and Jamaat-i-Islami would also be invited to the moot, but the ruling PML-N and its ally in the Centre, Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan, would not be extended an invitation.
The TTAP has also formed a six-member committee to hold consultations with political parties and reach an agreement on the agenda for the proposed MPC.

deduped_items.body_text:
ISLAMABAD: Minister for Finance and Revenue Muhammad Aurangzeb held a kick-off meeting on Tuesday with a visiting staff mission of the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
The IMF mission, led by Iva Petrova, is in Islamabad for the fourth review of Pakistan’s $7 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) arrangement and the third review of the $1.4bn Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF).
Aurangzeb, in a virtual meeting, briefed the IMF team on the latest macroeconomic indicators, improvements in credit rating and overall investment climate amid a challenging outlook emanating from prolonged Iran conflict.
On the successful conclusion of talks, Pakistan will be entitled to disbursement of about $1.2bn under the two programmes: $1bn under the EFF and $200 million under the RSF by the end of October or early November, but may require waivers from the IMF’s executive board for slippages on structural benchmarks.
The authorities are in continuous breach of structural benchmarks regarding the sovereign wealth fund (SWF) law that was originally missed in March.
The federal government already notified new procurement rules on Monday, two days ahead of the deadline, ie, Sept 30.
The SWF law is part of the discussions with the visiting IMF team. Authorities are in breach of an end-March 2026 structural benchmark on amendments to the Sovereign Wealth Fund Act to adopt governance mechanisms and safeguards for seven state-owned enterprises (SOEs), involving an asset portfolio of about $8bn.
Most of them are blue-chip entities listed on the stock exchange but remain outside normal reporting requirements. They include OGDCL, Pakistan Petroleum Limited (PPL), Mari Petroleum, National Bank of Pakistan (NBP), Govt Holdings, Pakistan Development Fund, and the Neelum-Jhelum Hydropower project. The amendments are pending parliamentary approval.
The IMF team has been in Pakistan since Sept 23. It spent the initial days in Karachi for engagements with the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) and other stakeholders.
The staff mission has so far held engagements with officials from SBP, the finance ministry, the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR), the Establishment Division, and the finance secretaries of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Punjab.
New procurement rules
Against this backdrop, the government notified the Public Procurement Rules 2026 to promote greater transparency and competition in public procurement while keeping certain exemptions for direct contracting with SOEs and limiting the bidding to national firms.
The IMF had certain reservations over the preferential treatment of SOEs for direct contracting.
Rule 32 of the new rules provides that a procuring agency may engage through EPADS (E-Pak Acquisition and Disposal System, a digital system developed and enforced by the Public Procurement Regulatory Authority) to manage and administer the process of procurement in direct contracting with SOEs for the procurement of such works and services, including consultancy services, which are time-sensitive, scattered, remotely located and in the public interest or in case of urgency and provided they do not sub-let those contracts initiated prior to the commencement of the new rules continuing under the 2004 framework.
The new rules make the use of EPADS mandatory for public procurement and disposal by federal procuring agencies, provide for the establishment of dedicated procurement cells, and introduce mechanisms to discourage conflicts of interest through third-party validation, evaluation, and pre-shipment inspection for large procurements.
The new rules further strengthen the enforcement mechanism through the provision of blacklisting and cross-debarment, independent grievance redressal committees with an appellate mechanism at PPRA to clearly identify material deviations and mis-procurement, including deliberate procurement outside EPADS, failure to constitute prescribed committees, tailor-made specifications, violation of advertisement and response-time require

LAHORE: A judicial magistrate on Tuesday allowed Defence C police a six-day physical remand of two suspects in a case against them over the alleged gang-rape of an Azeri woman.
The 20-year-old Azerbaijan national had travelled to Pakistan for business purposes and was allegedly gang-raped by three men in a rented flat of a private housing society located near Raiwind on the night between Friday and Saturday.
One of the prime suspects had been arrested on Monday, while another’s arrest surfaced on Tuesday. According to Lahore Deputy Inspector General (Investigation) Zeeshan Raza, police had identified the third suspect and were conducting raids to trace him.
On Tuesday, the police produced the two arrested men before Magistrate Azhar Mahmood at Cantonment Courts.
The investigating officer sought their 14-day physical remand for interrogation, collection of evidence and DNA examination.
However, the magistrate approved a six-day physical remand of the suspects.
Separately, a session’s court granted interim pre-arrest bail to a female suspect in the case, restraining police from arresting her till Oct 5.
The Azeri woman had mentioned in her application to the police that two women had approached her for dinner and later they went to a cafe, where the three men accused of raping her had met them.
One of the two women who allegedly approached the victim appeared before the court along with her lawyer on Tuesday.
The lawyer argued that his client had been implicated in the case with mala fide intention. He said she wanted to join police investigation to prove her innocence.
He further expressed fear that she would be arrested and requested the court to approve are pre-arrest bail.
The court granted the suspect bail till Oct 5, with the directive to join the police investigation before the next hearing.
Woman says suspects told her to drink alcohol
The judicial proceedings came a day after the foreign woman recorded her statement before Judicial Magistrate Muhammad Sagheer under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC).
Police Sub-Inspector Faryal Malik, the investigating officer, had produced the woman before the magistrate under strict security arrangements.
In her statement, a copy of which is available with Dawn, the woman said she had arrived in Islamabad from Istanbul on Sept 13 and stayed in Faisalabad for five days before travelling to Lahore.
“I had a plan to visit Skardu, but I could not go there because I was alone,” she said.
According to her, on the day of the alleged incident, she messaged two women, asking them to meet her in Lahore. At around 11pm, she went to a cafe where she met one of them and later accompanied her to a house in Bahria Town to meet the other.
The complainant told the magistrate that at around 2am, a white car arrived carrying two men, one of whom was sent on remand on Tuesday (first suspect).
Later, they moved to an apartment where two more men arrived, one of whom was the second person sent on remand (second suspect), while she did not know the name of the other man.
According to the complainant, in a separate room, one of the women took between Rs20,000 and Rs30,000 from the first suspect, saying the money was for a party, while the second woman also joined them.
The Azeri woman said she made it clear that she “did not need money or alcohol”. She alleged that the first suspect tried to touch her and locked her in a separate room.
When she asked about her friends, she was told that they had left. When she tried to leave, the complainant said she was told that she could not go because her friends had taken money.
The victim said she offered to pay the men, but they told her that she would have to drink alcohol with them before they would let her go.
She alleged that the three men raped her.
She further stated that the suspects then put her in a car and threw her out at an unknown location, while threatening her with dire consequences if she approached the police.

For its part, the PPP said it “welcomes the move” and would forward the invitation to the party’s chairperson, Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari. The TTAP would then be informed of his stance.
The development was confirmed in separate but similar statements by the two sides.
The opposition had first announced its intention to hold a multiparty moot on Sept 11, with the PTI leading the initiative. PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan had outlined plans to hold the conference, saying that “the current law and order situation, the economy, inflation, lawlessness, and the creation of new provinces issue” called for such measures.
His statement to the media came after a meeting with Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) leaders, who have agreed to attend the opposition’s moot.
A delegation of the TTAP, led by Barrister Gohar, called on PPP Secretary General Nayyar Hussain Bukhari at the party’s Central Secretariat in Islamabad and formally invited his party to the moot as well, statements by the two sides said.
The delegation also included Leader of Opposition in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, Senator Zeeshan Akhunzada and TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Yousafzai.

Yousafzai said Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam (JUI), Awami National Party (ANP) and Jamaat-i-Islami would also be invited to the moot, but the ruling PML-N and its ally in the Centre, Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan, would not be extended an invitation.

deduped_items.title: Soaring cancer rates emerge as a key US midterms issue
deduped_items.body_text:
Soaring cancer rates emerge as a key US midterms issue
- By Reuters -
- Sep 29, 2026
Pacing a stage at the Iowa State Fair, flanked by his wife and four of their six children, Republican US Congressman Zach Nunn spoke passionately about an issue that has emerged as a key concern in his competitive midterms race: cancer.
“Look, my mom is a survivor. I know that it has touched all of us, our family, our friends,” he said at the August event, touting his efforts to bring more money for cancer screening to Iowa’s third congressional district.
Two days before, his Democratic challenger in November’s election, state Senator Sarah Trone Garriott, had discussed cancer on the same stage.
“We know Iowa has a cancer problem. All of us have friends, neighbors, maybe we’ve even experienced it ourselves,” she said.
They were not the only hopefuls to talk about it: five of the six House, Senate and gubernatorial candidates who appeared at the fair discussed Iowa’s high cancer rates, reflecting the extent to which the disease has become a bipartisan campaign issue this year.
Candidates, advocacy groups and strategists say the state’s rising cancer rate – the second highest in the country behind Kentucky – has for the first time emerged as a major issue alongside kitchen-table concerns such as the cost of living.
While the causes of cancer are often complex and not well understood, Iowa voters’ concerns are driven in part by worries that the state’s worsening water pollution from nitrates and other chemicals may be to blame for a spike in cases.
Every major candidate in Iowa’s competitive races for Congress and the state governorship has talked about their plans to tackle cancer in recent speeches, social media posts or on their websites, according to a Reuters review of campaign materials.
The candidates have pledged a range of actions from increasing cancer screening to improving water quality monitoring. Democrats have used the issue to push for expanded healthcare access, while Republicans have promoted greater treatment options and research funding.
After more than a decade of decline, Iowa’s cancer rate began to rise in 2014, and it has had the second-highest cancer rate in the nation since 2023, according to reports by the Iowa Cancer Registry, which tracks and studies cancer cases among Iowans.
It is one of just three states where cancer is rising, driven by higher rates of lung, prostate and breast cancers, among others, according to the National Cancer Institute at the National Institutes of Health.
Tim Hagle, a political scientist at the University of Iowa, said he can’t remember cancer ever being such a significant concern in past elections. The issue has taken hold in part this year because it ties into voter concern about other health issues, like Republican-backed cuts to Medicaid, the federal health program for lower-income Americans, he said.
THE POLITICS OF CANCER
Some Democrats are using the focus on cancer to attack incumbent Republicans for supporting President Donald Trump’s 2025 tax and spending law, which made cuts to Medicaid by expanding work requirements for beneficiaries, among other changes.
Josh Turek, a Democrat running for Senate, in his remarks at the Iowa State Fair criticized his Republican opponent Ashley Hinson, who represents Iowa’s second congressional district, for “(voting) for 110,000 Iowans to lose their healthcare in a state with a cancer and a healthcare crisis.”
Independent health policy research group KFF estimates that around 100,000 Iowans could lose health insurance by 2034 due to changes under Trump’s tax and spending law.
Hinson pointed to her support for legislation that would improve access to mobile cancer screening and mammogram machines in rural areas, and for conservation efforts to improve water quality.
“I have lost two aunts and my grandmother to cancer. It’s personal to me,” she said in an email to Reuters.

deduped_items.title: Female biryani vendor accuses Karachi police of forcing her out of her home
deduped_items.body_text:
Female biryani vendor accuses Karachi police of forcing her out of her home
- By Asif Khan -
- Sep 29, 2026
A woman who sets up a biryani cart to earn a living has accused police at the Korangi Industrial Area police station of forcibly throw out from her home late at night.
The woman said her belongings were thrown out onto the street and that she had been left sitting outside with her possessions since around 3 AM.
According to the woman, she had been living in the property for the past eight months. She said she sells biryani from a roadside stall to support herself.
She also alleged that the station house officer (SHO) and a female police officer had taken a Rs.70,000 bribe to evict her from her home.
The woman said she was removed from the house because she had been unable to pay two months’ rent.
She is now calling for an investigation into the allegations against officers at the Korangi Industrial Area police station.

deduped_items.title: Govt likely to reduce petrol price today
deduped_items.body_text:
Govt likely to reduce petrol price today
- By Aleem Malik -
- Sep 29, 2026
ISLAMABAD: The government will likely reduce petroleum prices for a second consecutive day today, as oil prices have declined in the international market, ARY News reported.
Fuel prices may be slashed for September 30, with estimates suggesting that petrol could drop by Rs 1.50 and diesel by Rs 2.73 per litre.
Oil prices declined on Tuesday as investors focused on signs of recovering crude exports from the region and lingering concerns over Middle East supply disruptions arising from the US-Israeli war on Iran.
Brent crude futures were down 54 cents, or 0.51%, at $104.74 a barrel at 11:44 GMT. Meanwhile, US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude was at $91.83, down 77 cents, or 0.83%.
Brent and WTI are headed for monthly gains of around 16% and 7%, respectively.
Yesterday, the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) has issued a notification announcing a reduction in petrol and diesel prices for the next fortnight.
According to the notification, the price of petrol has been reduced by Rs 2.27 per litre, bringing the new price to Rs 389.03 per litre.
The price of high-speed diesel has been reduced by Rs 3.56 per litre, with the new price set at Rs 404.97 per litre.

deduped_items.body_text:
ISLAMABAD: Opposition alliance Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) on Tuesday invited the PPP, a key ally of the ruling PML-N in the Centre, to attend multiparty conference that is being planned by the opposition.
For its part, the PPP said it “welcomes the move” and would forward the invitation to the party’s chairperson, Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari. The TTAP would then be informed of his stance.
The development was confirmed in separate but similar statements by the two sides.
The opposition had first announced its intention to hold a multiparty moot on Sept 11, with the PTI leading the initiative. PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan had outlined plans to hold the conference, saying that “the current law and order situation, the economy, inflation, lawlessness, and the creation of new provinces issue” called for such measures.
His statement to the media came after a meeting with Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) leaders, who have agreed to attend the opposition’s moot.
A delegation of the TTAP, led by Barrister Gohar, called on PPP Secretary General Nayyar Hussain Bukhari at the party’s Central Secretariat in Islamabad and formally invited his party to the moot as well, statements by the two sides said.
The delegation also included Leader of Opposition in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, Senator Zeeshan Akhunzada and TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Yousafzai.
The TTAP delegation briefed Bukhari on the objectives and purpose of the planned multiparty conference, the statements said.
They also discussed the political situation in the country, supremacy of the Constitution, strengthening of democratic institutions, contacts between political parties and other matters.
The statements quoted Bukhari as saying that the PPP considered “engagement and consultation with political parties on constitutional and democratic matters important”.
Speaking to Dawn after the meeting, TTAP spokesperson Yousafzai said the multiparty conference would be held after PTI’s protest, which is scheduled for Oct 4 to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan.
“We have started meeting with the representatives of political parties so that the date and venue for the moot is finalised,” he said, adding that since the PPP had taken a clear stance over the creation of new provinces, the opposition had decided to invite it as well.
In the recent past, the proposal for the creation of new administrative units was first floated by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi in July. The proposition drew strong reactions from government ministers, while the country’s leading lawyers’ bodies adopted divergent positions.
The PPP, which rules Sindh, has strongly opposed any division of the province and maintains that any decision to create new provinces must be taken through the constitutional and parliamentary process and with political consensus.
Meanwhile, the relationship between the PPP and the PML-N had also been strained lately during acrimonious election campaigns in Azad Jammu and Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan.
The TTAP also plans invite other parties to the opposition’s moot.
Yousafzai said Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam (JUI), Awami National Party (ANP) and Jamaat-i-Islami would also be invited to the moot, but the ruling PML-N and its ally in the Centre, Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan, would not be extended an invitation.
The TTAP has also formed a six-member committee to hold consultations with political parties and reach an agreement on the agenda for the proposed MPC.

deduped_items.body_text:
ISLAMABAD: Opposition alliance Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) on Tuesday invited the PPP, a key ally of the ruling PML-N in the Centre, to attend multiparty conference that is being planned by the opposition.
For its part, the PPP said it “welcomes the move” and would forward the invitation to the party’s chairperson, Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari. The TTAP would then be informed of his stance.
The development was confirmed in separate but similar statements by the two sides.
The opposition had first announced its intention to hold a multiparty moot on Sept 11, with the PTI leading the initiative. PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan had outlined plans to hold the conference, saying that “the current law and order situation, the economy, inflation, lawlessness, and the creation of new provinces issue” called for such measures.
His statement to the media came after a meeting with Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) leaders, who have agreed to attend the opposition’s moot.
A delegation of the TTAP, led by Barrister Gohar, called on PPP Secretary General Nayyar Hussain Bukhari at the party’s Central Secretariat in Islamabad and formally invited his party to the moot as well, statements by the two sides said.
The delegation also included Leader of Opposition in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, Senator Zeeshan Akhunzada and TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Yousafzai.
The TTAP delegation briefed Bukhari on the objectives and purpose of the planned multiparty conference, the statements said.
They also discussed the political situation in the country, supremacy of the Constitution, strengthening of democratic institutions, contacts between political parties and other matters.
The statements quoted Bukhari as saying that the PPP considered “engagement and consultation with political parties on constitutional and democratic matters important”.
Speaking to Dawn after the meeting, TTAP spokesperson Yousafzai said the multiparty conference would be held after PTI’s protest, which is scheduled for Oct 4 to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan.
“We have started meeting with the representatives of political parties so that the date and venue for the moot is finalised,” he said, adding that since the PPP had taken a clear stance over the creation of new provinces, the opposition had decided to invite it as well.
In the recent past, the proposal for the creation of new administrative units was first floated by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi in July. The proposition drew strong reactions from government ministers, while the country’s leading lawyers’ bodies adopted divergent positions.
The PPP, which rules Sindh, has strongly opposed any division of the province and maintains that any decision to create new provinces must be taken through the constitutional and parliamentary process and with political consensus.
Meanwhile, the relationship between the PPP and the PML-N had also been strained lately during acrimonious election campaigns in Azad Jammu and Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan.
The TTAP also plans invite other parties to the opposition’s moot.
Yousafzai said Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam (JUI), Awami National Party (ANP) and Jamaat-i-Islami would also be invited to the moot, but the ruling PML-N and its ally in the Centre, Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan, would not be extended an invitation.
The TTAP has also formed a six-member committee to hold consultations with political parties and reach an agreement on the agenda for the proposed MPC.

The request is their second in just a few months, following a dispute over the extent of the ministry’s […] The post Supply Ministry postpones bread price review amid ongoing pu
deduped_items.body_text:
Supply Ministry postpones bread price review amid ongoing push from bakeries, mills          
        Supply Minister Sherif Farouk has asked for a week’s review period before the ministry responds to a request to raise its guideline consumer prices for two categories of non-subsidized bread, according to a source who was present at a Sunday meeting where representatives from bakeries and mills put forward their request.
The request is their second in just a few months, following a dispute over the extent of the ministry’s role in setting and enforcing non-subsidized bread prices.
Their push for higher guideline prices comes as the industry’s production costs rise steadily, with wheat prices spiralling again amid an escalation in the intensity of Russia’s war on Ukraine, and as domestic fuel prices continue to rise against the backdrop of the regional war.
Farouk said the ministry would review price movements over the coming week, and, if prices did not fall over that period, the ministry would revise guideline prices for the tourist and fino bread categories, the source said. The ministry did not commit to a specific percentage increase.
Senior representatives of the General Bakeries Division raised the issue of production costs at the meeting and called for a review of tourist and fino bread prices, proposing a 15 percent increase.
Milling sector representatives also presented an update on the wheat and flour markets and recent pressures on production costs, particularly higher maritime shipping and logistics costs and rising global wheat prices amid the shipping disruptions in the Black Sea.
Imported wheat reached record prices at the beginning of this week, rising to between LE16,600 and LE16,800 for Ukrainian wheat and LE17,000 for Russian wheat, compared with a maximum of LE12,200 to LE12,500 per ton in June.
Bakeries selling tourist bread rely on the free market for their flour supplies, which account for more than 50 percent of production costs, the source said. Transport and other operating costs have also risen, leaving bakeries facing significant losses.
The meeting is the latest in a series of calls bakeries have made to the ministry regarding tourist and fino bread prices, which intensified in August as flour and other production costs increased.
The Supply Ministry did not respond to the demands, issuing a directive instead on August 4 to maintain the prices and weights for tourist and fino bread set in March.
As bakeries continued to call for price increases, sources in the sector questioned the legal basis for the imposition of mandatory pricing on tourist bread, whose production inputs are not subsidized.
Lawyer Khaled Ali previously told Mada Masr however that since wheat is a “strategic commodity,” the ministry has a role in market oversight.
The ministry also threatened legal action against violators of its price directives at the time, with Interior Ministry statements later announcing “large scale campaigns to control supply crimes” against those violating Supply Ministry decisions on prices and weights.
The changes in wheat and flour prices come amid volatility in global wheat markets, particularly continued tensions in the Black Sea region, the main source of Egypt’s wheat imports. Import data for the first eight months of the year showed that Russia and Ukraine together accounted for more than 82 percent of Egypt’s wheat imports, despite repeated announcements by the Supply Ministry of plans to diversify import origins.

Govt tells BP it would block sale of company’s Egypt assets to Energean          
        The government informed British Petroleum it would reject a deal that would see the British company sell some of its Egypt based oil and gas assets to Israeli majority-owned Energean, according to two sources informed of the deal who spoke to Mada Masr on condition of anonymity, one of whom who works for the company.
The stance was communicated during a meeting in Cairo on Thursday between Petroleum Minister Karim Badawy and BP Executive Vice President Gordon Birrell, they said.
One reason the government gave for rejecting the potential deal was “national security imperatives,” according to the BP source. Other concerns relate to the wide gap in technical capabilities between the two companies, particularly in deep water drilling, an area where Energean’s capacity is comparatively limited, the source said.
The meeting came as BP seeks to divest part of its energy asset portfolio in Egypt, while the government is pushing to attract more investment into the petroleum sector in order to raise natural gas production amid a major energy shortfall.
Media reports have pointed to exclusive talks between BP and Energean over the latter’s purchase of some of BP’s assets in Egypt, although no deal has been officially announced.
Any change in ownership of oil fields between producing companies requires the approval of the government, represented by the Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation. EGPC holds pre-emption rights, with agreements between companies and the government stipulating that any transfer of rights must first be offered to EGPC or receive its approval before being transferred to a third party, according to the two sources, as well as to a former EGPC official and former head of the Electricity Utility and Consumer Protection Regulatory Agency, Hafez al-Salmawy.
The BP source anticipated that the company’s next move could see it officially announce the deal and its talks with Energean on Wednesday, despite knowing that Egypt intends to reject it. But BP also has the option to wait until it has a clearer picture, the source said.
If BP does reach a final agreement with the Israeli company, it will have to formally apply to the Egyptian government, through EGPC, for approval as a condition of completing the deal.
According to the second informed source, an official announcement from BP would act as a maneuver to pressure EGPC, as it would clearly mark the assets covered by the deal as up for sale, something that might hold up further investment decisions for those assets. This would be particularly sensitive in the case of the Temsah concession, which includes the Denise West field, where a finding of an estimated two trillion cubic meters of natural gas reserves was announced earlier this year.
The government is undertaking a push at present to increase domestic gas production, which has fallen to its lowest level in a decade, while domestic demand continues to grow. Gas prices have also risen significantly, putting pressure on the state budget.
Reuters cited informed sources to report at the end of August that BP, which produces around 60 percent of Egypt’s natural gas, had entered exclusive talks with Energean to acquire the assets the British company wants to sell. The potential deal has since sparked broad controversy, including questions submitted by several members of Parliament to the Petroleum Ministry.
The lawmakers specifically sought reassurances regarding Energean’s “financial solvency, technical expertise and operational capacity,” to ensure that the new foreign partner would be able to inject enough to finance the drilling and development programs required of it at the Egyptian fields.

deduped_items.title: Moscow Wants Ukraine to ‘Pay the Price’ as Russian Drones Rain Down on Central Kyiv
deduped_items.summary: Putin’s spokesperson Dmitry Peskov threatened Kyiv on Monday, saying it will “pay a price” for unspecified actions over the past few months, while also saying the Russian military had been told to hit anything they see fit. The statement came amid unprecedented strikes on central Kyiv in recent days and a broader escalation throughout September against civilian infrastructure, ranging from passenger trains and gas stations, to educational institutions and data centers.

deduped_items.title: Плющенко-младший набрал минимум для юниорского чемпионата мира
deduped_items.body_text:
Александр Плющенко набрал технический минимум для участия в юниорском чемпионате мира по фигурному катанию. Об этом сообщает Sports.ru со ссылкой на его мать Яну Рудковскую.
Фигурист выполнил требование благодаря выступлениям на этапах Гран-при среди юниоров. Кроме чемпионата мира, планируется участие еще в трех международных турнирах, но их названия пока не раскрываются.
«Благодаря участию в этапах Гран-при Александр уже набрал технический минимум для участия в чемпионате мира среди юниоров. Кроме участия там мы планируем, что он выступит еще на трех международных стартах до него. Чуть позже станет понятно, что это будут за турниры», — заявила Рудковская.
Александр Плющенко — сын генерального директора и совладелицы академии «Ангелы Плющенко» Яны Рудковской и олимпийского чемпиона Евгения Плющенко. Спортсмен выступает за Азербайджан. В текущем сезоне он дебютировал на этапах Гран-при среди юниоров, заняв 13-е место в Анкаре и десятое в Батуми.

deduped_items.title: Дудя арестовали из-за взятого интервью
deduped_items.body_text:
Суд заочно арестовал журналиста Юрия Дудя (внесен Минюстом России в реестр иноагентов, внесен в список террористов и экстремистов Росфинмониторинга) из-за интервью с лидером воюющего на стороне Украины «Русского добровольческого корпуса» (РДК, запрещенная в России террористическая организация) Денисом Капустиным (внесен в России в перечень террористов и экстремистов). Об этом «Ленте.ру» рассказали в Следственном комитете России.
Капустин также заочно арестован.
В ведомстве сообщили, что не позднее апреля в Молдове журналист записал интервью, в котором оправдывался и пропагандировал терроризм. Далее Дудь опубликовал этот ролик на администрируемом им канале на видеохостинге YouTube.

deduped_items.title: В поставках нефти с Ближнего Востока наметился перелом
deduped_items.body_text:
В сентябре 2026 года экспорт нефти с Ближнего Востока резко вырос, приблизившись к тому уровню, который наблюдался до закрытия Ираном Ормузского пролива. Об этом сообщило The New York Times (NYT).
Предполагается, что это восстановление может ослабить давление на мировые цены на энергоносители. Издание сослалось на данные компании Kpler, согласно которым в первом месяце осени через Ормузский пролив ежедневно проходило в среднем 10 миллионов баррелей нефти. Через трубопроводы и порты, обходящие пролив, ежедневно из стран Персидского залива вывозилось шесть миллионов баррелей сырой нефти. До начала войны с Ираном в конце февраля из региона ежедневно по морю и другими путями вывозилось около 19 миллионов баррелей нефти.
Есть мнение, что увеличение экспорта нефти свидетельствует о возможном ослаблении контроля Ирана над этим водным путем.

deduped_items.title: "Успех Путина". В Италии пришли к неожиданному для Европы выводу о России
deduped_items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- Попытки Запада нанести поражение России привели к консолидации российского общества и росту поддержки президента Владимира Путина, пишет итальянская газета IL Fatto Quotidiano.
- Автор статьи отмечает, что успех на выборах в Госдуму подтверждает рост популярности российского лидера.
МОСКВА, 29 сен – РИА Новости. Попытки Запада нанести поражение России привели к консолидации российского общества и росту поддержки президента Владимира Путина, пишет итальянская газета IL Fatto Quotidiano.
"Успех <…> на выборах в Госдуму, где он побил все предыдущие рекорды, подтверждает верность этого прогноза", — говорится в статье.
Автор также указывает, что итальянская правящая элита пытается скрыть собственную несостоятельность, внушая гражданам мифы о ненависти россиян к своей стране. По его мнению, подобные утверждения абсурдны: россияне любят родину и негативно относятся к западным политикам, которые стремятся обречь их на нищету и поражение.
По итогам выборов в российскую Государственную Думу девятого созыва прошли пять политических партий. Правящая "Единая Россия" получила рекордное число депутатских мест - 349 из 450.
Выборы проходили в России с 18 по 20 сентября. В новый созыв избрались представители пяти политических партий: "Единая Россия", КПРФ, ЛДПР, "Новые люди" и "Справедливая Россия", а также представитель партии "Родина" и четыре самовыдвиженца.
Полный текст статьи читайте на сайте ИноСМИ >>

deduped_items.title: В Армении задержали известного драматурга за пост в соцсети
deduped_items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- Следственный комитет Армении сообщил о задержании известного армянского драматурга, актера и сценариста Ваграма Саакяна за пост в соцсети.
- Саакян опубликовал пост, который, по утверждению ведомства, содержит призывы к ненависти, нетерпимости, вражде и их пропаганду.
- В отношении Саакяна было инициировано уголовное преследование по статье о публичных высказываниях, направленных на возбуждение или пропаганду ненависти, нетерпимости или вражды.
ЕРЕВАН, 29 сен - РИА Новости. Следственный комитет Армении сообщил о задержании известного армянского драматурга, актера и сценариста Ваграма Саакяна за пост в соцсети Facebook*. 
В ведомстве утверждают, что 8 января 2025 года Саакян опубликовал на своей странице в соцсети публикацию, якобы содержащую призывы к ненависти, нетерпимости, вражде и их пропаганду. 
В Армении демонтируется фундамент государственности, заявил Кочарян
20 сентября, 22:49
"Согласно заключению экспертизы, полученному 1 сентября 2026 года, подтверждено, что в публикации В.С. (Ваграма Саакяна -ред.) содержится ненависть. 29 сентября решением прокурора в его отношении было инициировано уголовное преследование по статье "Публичные высказывания, направленные на возбуждение или пропаганду ненависти, нетерпимости или вражды, а также распространение с этой целью материалов с использованием публично демонстрируемых произведений, средств массовой информации или информационно-коммуникационных технологий". Он задержан", - говорится в сообщении.
* Деятельность Meta (соцсети Facebook и Instagram) запрещена в России как экстремистская
В Совбезе предупредили Армению о возможном разочаровании

deduped_items.title: МВД предложило усилить контроль за автошколами с дистанционным обучением
deduped_items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- МВД России предложило обязать автошколы сообщать Госавтоинспекции об использовании дистанционных образовательных технологий при обучении.
- Автошколы также должны будут предоставлять в ГАИ сведения о сетевой форме обучения в случае ее применения.
- Ведомство предложило сократить срок для проведения повторного обследования автошкол, не прошедших первоначальную проверку, с шести месяцев до трех.
МОСКВА, 29 сен - РИА Новости. МВД России предложило обязать автошколы сообщать Госавтоинспекции об использовании дистанционных образовательных технологий при обучении, говорится в проекте приказа ведомства, опубликованном на сайте проектов нормативных правовых актов. 
"Для получения заключения организация представляет в подразделение Госавтоинспекции заявление... содержащее... сведения о применении организацией электронного обучения, дистанционных образовательных технологий при реализации программ профессионального обучения с указанием наименования программного обеспечения, используемого в составе дистанционных образовательных технологий, и номера реестровой записи в едином реестре российских программ для электронных вычислительных машин и баз данных", - говорится в документе проекта приказа. 
Кроме того, согласно документу, автошколы также должны будут предоставлять в ГАИ сведения о сетевой форме обучения в случае ее применения. 
Также в ведомстве предложили сократить срок для проведения повторного обследования автошкол, которые не прошли первоначальную проверку - с шести месяцев до трех. 
Планируется, что приказ вступит в силу 1 марта 2027 года.
Юрист рассказала, как будут оценивать автошколы в России
9 марта, 02:49

deduped_items.title: UK PM Burnham seeks 'hope again' at Labour Party conference
deduped_items.summary: Andy Burnham is seeking a delicate balance between optimism and realism at Labour's annual party conference. He promised hope and an end to "politics as usual" but also an "honest conversation" about difficult dilemmas.
deduped_items.body_text:
UK PM Burnham seeks 'hope again' at Labour Party conference
September 29, 2026
Andy Burnham is seeking a delicate balance between optimism and realism at Labour's annual party conference. He promised hope and an end to "politics as usual" but also an "honest conversation" about difficult dilemmas.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, only in the role for a few months after replacing Keir Starmer, has told the Labour Party conference in his native Liverpool that his government wants to restore hope and end "politics as usual."
But the UK's seventh prime minister in a decade is trying to balance a series of evidently conflicting fiscal goals: bolstering economic growth, reducing cost-of-living pressures, safeguarding pensions and making care costs more affordable, upgrading creaking infrastructure and significantly boosting military spending.
That's all while battling a populist challenge from Reform UK and Restore Britain on the right and the Green Party on the left. This led Labour to severe local and regional election defeats in May and ultimately spelt his predecessor Starmer's demise.
What did Burnham say in his conference speech?
Burnham, a Liverpool lad who was mayor of Manchester prior to moving to take up Britain's top political job, repeated his most common mantra since coming to power, namely that "more of the same" will not solve the various issues facing the UK.
"We can't carry on as we are. Politics as usual has taken Britain backwards," Burnham said. "More of the same isn't good enough and isn't going to get us where we need to be."
The conference's banner headline "hope again" was not incompatible with a more honest conversation, Burnham said.
"Hope comes from honesty ... and saying the things politicians usually avoid," he said.
He cited Labour's post-war government under Clement Atlee, famed for achievements like setting up Britain's National Health Service, as an example of his party past credentials, having "built the peace" in the public interest. He said that since the 1980s and the Conservative-dominated Margaret Thatcher era of his youth, this direction was lost.
"I will say it straight, Britain has been on the wrong path for a long time. Deindustrialization, deregulation, privatization, austerity, Brexit, and what has it given us? A country run for vested interests, not in the public interest — with power held in too few hands, and too many places left to drift," Burnham said.
Burnham told the audience he would take on "the difficult issues that have been ignored for too long," including social care, high levels of youth unemployment, and greater public control of once-nationalized core interests like energy, water and housing.
"The British right talk about 'taking back control," Burnham said, evoking the slogan of the 2016 Brexit campaign. "Never forget that they are the ones who gave it away in the first place!"
Why is Burnham, and Britain, in such a tricky bind?
Burnham said on coming to power that he wanted his premiership to be a "circuit-breaker for Britain" after years of rising prices and anemic growth.
He hit the ground with a handful of new policies like a cap on bus fares, temporarily removing value added tax from electricity bills amid the Iran war, and announcing a bid to stamp out rough sleeping.
But critics say his more grand stated strategy lacks detail and could prove economically unfeasible.
Burnham is constrained by a series of factors, including Labour's 2024 election campaign pledges under Starmer's leadership, Britain's strained public finances, and the suddenly risk-averse debt markets that have started heaping pressure on most developed economies of late.
Borrowing costs for his UK government, as it eyes a series of new banner spending plans, hit a 10-year-high on the morning of Burnham's speech.
In a sign of this lacking spending wiggle room, Burnham has already pushed back his stated aim to formulate reform plans for Britain's social care system.

deduped_items.summary: Andy Burnham is seeking a delicate balance between optimism and realism at Labour's annual party conference. He promised hope and an end to "politics as usual" but also an "honest conversation" about difficult dilemmas.
deduped_items.body_text:
UK PM Burnham seeks 'hope again' at Labour Party conference
September 29, 2026
Andy Burnham is seeking a delicate balance between optimism and realism at Labour's annual party conference. He promised hope and an end to "politics as usual" but also an "honest conversation" about difficult dilemmas.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, only in the role for a few months after replacing Keir Starmer, has told the Labour Party conference in his native Liverpool that his government wants to restore hope and end "politics as usual."
But the UK's seventh prime minister in a decade is trying to balance a series of evidently conflicting fiscal goals: bolstering economic growth, reducing cost-of-living pressures, safeguarding pensions and making care costs more affordable, upgrading creaking infrastructure and significantly boosting military spending.
That's all while battling a populist challenge from Reform UK and Restore Britain on the right and the Green Party on the left. This led Labour to severe local and regional election defeats in May and ultimately spelt his predecessor Starmer's demise.
What did Burnham say in his conference speech?
Burnham, a Liverpool lad who was mayor of Manchester prior to moving to take up Britain's top political job, repeated his most common mantra since coming to power, namely that "more of the same" will not solve the various issues facing the UK.
"We can't carry on as we are. Politics as usual has taken Britain backwards," Burnham said. "More of the same isn't good enough and isn't going to get us where we need to be."
The conference's banner headline "hope again" was not incompatible with a more honest conversation, Burnham said.
"Hope comes from honesty ... and saying the things politicians usually avoid," he said.
He cited Labour's post-war government under Clement Atlee, famed for achievements like setting up Britain's National Health Service, as an example of his party past credentials, having "built the peace" in the public interest. He said that since the 1980s and the Conservative-dominated Margaret Thatcher era of his youth, this direction was lost.
"I will say it straight, Britain has been on the wrong path for a long time. Deindustrialization, deregulation, privatization, austerity, Brexit, and what has it given us? A country run for vested interests, not in the public interest — with power held in too few hands, and too many places left to drift," Burnham said.
Burnham told the audience he would take on "the difficult issues that have been ignored for too long," including social care, high levels of youth unemployment, and greater public control of once-nationalized core interests like energy, water and housing.
"The British right talk about 'taking back control," Burnham said, evoking the slogan of the 2016 Brexit campaign. "Never forget that they are the ones who gave it away in the first place!"
Why is Burnham, and Britain, in such a tricky bind?
Burnham said on coming to power that he wanted his premiership to be a "circuit-breaker for Britain" after years of rising prices and anemic growth.
He hit the ground with a handful of new policies like a cap on bus fares, temporarily removing value added tax from electricity bills amid the Iran war, and announcing a bid to stamp out rough sleeping.
But critics say his more grand stated strategy lacks detail and could prove economically unfeasible.
Burnham is constrained by a series of factors, including Labour's 2024 election campaign pledges under Starmer's leadership, Britain's strained public finances, and the suddenly risk-averse debt markets that have started heaping pressure on most developed economies of late.
Borrowing costs for his UK government, as it eyes a series of new banner spending plans, hit a 10-year-high on the morning of Burnham's speech.
In a sign of this lacking spending wiggle room, Burnham has already pushed back his stated aim to formulate reform plans for Britain's social care system.

deduped_items.title: UK PM Burnham seeks 'hope again' at Labour Party conference
deduped_items.summary: Andy Burnham is seeking a delicate balance between optimism and realism at Labour's annual party conference. He promised hope and an end to "politics as usual" but also an "honest conversation" about difficult dilemmas.
deduped_items.body_text:
UK PM Burnham seeks 'hope again' at Labour Party conference
September 29, 2026
Andy Burnham is seeking a delicate balance between optimism and realism at Labour's annual party conference. He promised hope and an end to "politics as usual" but also an "honest conversation" about difficult dilemmas.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham, only in the role for a few months after replacing Keir Starmer, has told the Labour Party conference in his native Liverpool that his government wants to restore hope and end "politics as usual."
But the UK's seventh prime minister in a decade is trying to balance a series of evidently conflicting fiscal goals: bolstering economic growth, reducing cost-of-living pressures, safeguarding pensions and making care costs more affordable, upgrading creaking infrastructure and significantly boosting military spending.
That's all while battling a populist challenge from Reform UK and Restore Britain on the right and the Green Party on the left. This led Labour to severe local and regional election defeats in May and ultimately spelt his predecessor Starmer's demise.
What did Burnham say in his conference speech?
Burnham, a Liverpool lad who was mayor of Manchester prior to moving to take up Britain's top political job, repeated his most common mantra since coming to power, namely that "more of the same" will not solve the various issues facing the UK.
"We can't carry on as we are. Politics as usual has taken Britain backwards," Burnham said. "More of the same isn't good enough and isn't going to get us where we need to be."
The conference's banner headline "hope again" was not incompatible with a more honest conversation, Burnham said.
"Hope comes from honesty ... and saying the things politicians usually avoid," he said.
He cited Labour's post-war government under Clement Atlee, famed for achievements like setting up Britain's National Health Service, as an example of his party past credentials, having "built the peace" in the public interest. He said that since the 1980s and the Conservative-dominated Margaret Thatcher era of his youth, this direction was lost.
"I will say it straight, Britain has been on the wrong path for a long time. Deindustrialization, deregulation, privatization, austerity, Brexit, and what has it given us? A country run for vested interests, not in the public interest — with power held in too few hands, and too many places left to drift," Burnham said.
Burnham told the audience he would take on "the difficult issues that have been ignored for too long," including social care, high levels of youth unemployment, and greater public control of once-nationalized core interests like energy, water and housing.
"The British right talk about 'taking back control," Burnham said, evoking the slogan of the 2016 Brexit campaign. "Never forget that they are the ones who gave it away in the first place!"
Why is Burnham, and Britain, in such a tricky bind?
Burnham said on coming to power that he wanted his premiership to be a "circuit-breaker for Britain" after years of rising prices and anemic growth.
He hit the ground with a handful of new policies like a cap on bus fares, temporarily removing value added tax from electricity bills amid the Iran war, and announcing a bid to stamp out rough sleeping.
But critics say his more grand stated strategy lacks detail and could prove economically unfeasible.
Burnham is constrained by a series of factors, including Labour's 2024 election campaign pledges under Starmer's leadership, Britain's strained public finances, and the suddenly risk-averse debt markets that have started heaping pressure on most developed economies of late.
Borrowing costs for his UK government, as it eyes a series of new banner spending plans, hit a 10-year-high on the morning of Burnham's speech.
In a sign of this lacking spending wiggle room, Burnham has already pushed back his stated aim to formulate reform plans for Britain's social care system.

deduped_items.title: Wahlsieg der Linkspartei in Berlin Warum konnte „Islamo-Gauchisme“ Regierungsprogramm werden?
deduped_items.summary: Die Linkspartei verdankt ihren Wahlsieg in Berlin einer starken Unterstützung muslimischer Wähler. Doch bereits am Wahlabend wird offensichtlich, wie weit die Verbindungen ins islamistische Milieu reichen. Dass sich der Islamo-Gauchisme bis ins Parlament ausbreitete, liegt aber auch an SPD, CDU und FDP. Ein Kommentar von Katja Adler. Dieser Beitrag Wahlsieg der Linkspartei in Berlin Warum konnte „Islamo-Gauchisme“ Regierungsprogramm werden? wurde veröffentlich auf JUNGE FREIHEIT.

deduped_items.title: Leone XIV: “IA e guerre, non possiamo restare a guardare. Serve il dialogo”
deduped_items.summary: Il pontefice sul volo da Metz a Roma, al termine del viaggio di quattro giorni in Francia: “Quanto all’estrema destra, sarebbe interessante studiare e analizzare se c’è un legame, e quale, tra la crescita di questi gruppi e una certa forma di religiosità che non costituiscono un'espressione autentica del cristianesimo. Possiamo tornare ai valori del Vangelo: non predica l’odio e la divisione”

deduped_items.title: "Solo italiani sul bus": a Fossano la denuncia di una 14enne marocchina, intervengono i carabinieri
deduped_items.summary: Una 14enne di origine marocchina, nata in Italia, denuncia di essere stata lasciata a terra a Fossano mentre cercava di salire, con regolare biglietto, su un bus sostitutivo diretto a Cuneo. L’autista le avrebbe detto: «Faccio salire solo gli italiani, non gli stranieri». L’uomo, affrontato successivamente dal fratello della ragazza, ha negato l’accusa sostenendo di essere stato frainteso e ha accennato delle scuse.
