deduped_items.title: Regeni, la forza del diritto e la reazione dei patrioti
deduped_items.summary: Ci sono voluti più di dieci anni, ma ieri il processo per il rapimento, le torture e la morte di Giulio Regeni è arrivato alla sentenza di primo grado. Gli imputati, tutti agenti degli apparati di sicurezza egiziani, erano quattro: uno è stato assolto, mentre agli è stata inflitta una pena di dieci anni per il sequestro e le torture. Una pena più lieve della richiesta della Procura, ma che ricostruisce finalmente la verità di quei terribili giorni, e stabilisce le responsabilità degli 007 egizia

deduped_items.title: Acampada en Sol por la vivienda, en directo | La ministra admite la dificultad de aprobar el decreto de renovación de alquileres
deduped_items.summary: El PSOE y Sumar acuerdan la protección frente a los desahucios hasta 2030 y la prórroga de los alquileres hasta 2028 | Las medidas se votarán en un pleno extraordinario en el Congreso este mismo viernes | El Sindicato de Inquilinas critica que el Gobierno haya dividido el decreto: “Todos los ojos están puestos en el texto”
deduped_items.body_text:
Acampada en Sol por la vivienda, en directo | Junts y Podemos no aclaran el sentido de su voto sobre los decretos de vivienda
El PSOE y Sumar acuerdan la protección frente a los desahucios hasta 2030 y la prórroga de los alquileres hasta 2028 | Las medidas se votarán en un pleno extraordinario en el Congreso el viernes
Momentos clave
Aprobados en el Consejo de ministros los dos Reales Decretos Leyes copn medidas de vivienda, el Gobierno queda ahora pendiente de su convalidación en el pleno convocado para este viernes. Junts y Podemos no han aclarado el sentido de su voto, a la espera de conocer el texto de las normas a las que ha dado a luz el Ejecutivo de PSOE y Sumar, si bien la formación morada critica la “trampa” de que las medidas hayan sido divididas en dos decretos. En el primero se incluyen medidas como la protección frente a desahucios hasta 2030, la regulación del alquiler de temporada y habitaciones, la prohibición de la compra de vivienda por parte de fondos buitre hasta 2028 o la prórroga de dos años de los contratos en vigor que finalizan antes del 31 de diciembre de 2028, así como medidas fiscales. En el segundo, solo va la prórroga automática de alquileres, una reclamación de Sumar que el Gobierno admite que “no se ha podido trabajar con los grupos políticos” tanto como el primero. Sumar señala que los decretos son “solo un primer paso” y anima a la ciudadanía a seguir presionando. Mientras, miles de manifestantes mantienen las acampadas de la Puerta del Sol de Madrid y otras ciudades para reclamar el fin de la especulación y los desahucios.
EL PAÍS ofrece de forma gratuita la última hora de la protesta contra la crisis de la vivienda. Si quieres apoyar nuestro periodismo, suscríbete.
Maricarmen vuelve a su casa. La mujer de 87 años ha aceptado el acuerdo que le ha ofrecido la empresa propietaria de su piso y volverá cuando salga del hospital Gregorio Marañón, donde ha estado ingresada desde hace seis días, cuando fue desahuciada de su piso donde ha vivido los últimos 71 años.
Podemos no aclara el sentido de su voto a los decretos de vivienda y pide al Gobierno que incluya las medidas en un solo paquete
La secretaria general de Podemos y diputada, Ione Belarra, ha catalogado como “una trampa” la división de las medidas sobre vivienda en dos reales decretos leyes que ha aprobado hoy el Consejo de Ministros: “El divide y vencerás no va a funcionar”.
Antes de entrar en el Pleno del Congreso, la dirigente morada no ha aclarado el sentido del voto de su formación y ha sostenido que el objetivo de lo acordado hoy es “lavar la cara al Gobierno y contener la movilización social”.
Belarra también ha animado a que “la gente se siga movilizando y organizando” y ha afirmado que la “única medida con un carácter mínimamente estructural”, en relación a la renovación automática de los alquileres, se incluye en un decreto que “el PSOE reconoce en privado que va a caer”.
Compromís lamenta que el Gobierno haya dividido en dos el ‘decreto Maricarmen’
Àgueda Micó, diputada de Compromís en el Grupo Mixto, ha afirmado este martes que “la primera decepción [sobre las medidas de vivienda] es que sean dos reales decretos y no uno”. La diputada ha indicado que a su partido “no le gustan” algunas medidas incluidas en los dos decretos aprobados por el Consejo de Ministros, como los beneficios que se le otorgarán a los caseros que bajen el precio del alquiler. “Hay que ver la letra pequeña”, ha destacado Micó en los pasillos del Congreso antes de ingresar al pleno.
Rodríguez lamenta que en vivienda “el PP ni está ni se le espera”
La ministra de Vivienda, Isabel Rodríguez, ha lamentado que el PP “ni está ni se le espera” en el problema de la vivienda, “el principal problema de los españoles”. En la rueda de prensa del Consejo de Ministros, ha destacado que los periodistas no le hayan planteado ninguna pregunta sobre el partido liderado por Alberto Núñez Feijóo. “Lamento es que en una situación como esta el principal partido de la oposición n

Acampada en Sol por la vivienda, en directo | Junts y Podemos no aclaran el sentido de su voto sobre los decretos de vivienda
El PSOE y Sumar acuerdan la protección frente a los desahucios hasta 2030 y la prórroga de los alquileres hasta 2028 | Las medidas se votarán en un pleno extraordinario en el Congreso el viernes
Momentos clave
Aprobados en el Consejo de ministros los dos Reales Decretos Leyes copn medidas de vivienda, el Gobierno queda ahora pendiente de su convalidación en el pleno convocado para este viernes. Junts y Podemos no han aclarado el sentido de su voto, a la espera de conocer el texto de las normas a las que ha dado a luz el Ejecutivo de PSOE y Sumar, si bien la formación morada critica la “trampa” de que las medidas hayan sido divididas en dos decretos. En el primero se incluyen medidas como la protección frente a desahucios hasta 2030, la regulación del alquiler de temporada y habitaciones, la prohibición de la compra de vivienda por parte de fondos buitre hasta 2028 o la prórroga de dos años de los contratos en vigor que finalizan antes del 31 de diciembre de 2028, así como medidas fiscales. En el segundo, solo va la prórroga automática de alquileres, una reclamación de Sumar que el Gobierno admite que “no se ha podido trabajar con los grupos políticos” tanto como el primero. Sumar señala que los decretos son “solo un primer paso” y anima a la ciudadanía a seguir presionando. Mientras, miles de manifestantes mantienen las acampadas de la Puerta del Sol de Madrid y otras ciudades para reclamar el fin de la especulación y los desahucios.
EL PAÍS ofrece de forma gratuita la última hora de la protesta contra la crisis de la vivienda. Si quieres apoyar nuestro periodismo, suscríbete.
Maricarmen vuelve a su casa. La mujer de 87 años ha aceptado el acuerdo que le ha ofrecido la empresa propietaria de su piso y volverá cuando salga del hospital Gregorio Marañón, donde ha estado ingresada desde hace seis días, cuando fue desahuciada de su piso donde ha vivido los últimos 71 años.
Podemos no aclara el sentido de su voto a los decretos de vivienda y pide al Gobierno que incluya las medidas en un solo paquete
La secretaria general de Podemos y diputada, Ione Belarra, ha catalogado como “una trampa” la división de las medidas sobre vivienda en dos reales decretos leyes que ha aprobado hoy el Consejo de Ministros: “El divide y vencerás no va a funcionar”.
Antes de entrar en el Pleno del Congreso, la dirigente morada no ha aclarado el sentido del voto de su formación y ha sostenido que el objetivo de lo acordado hoy es “lavar la cara al Gobierno y contener la movilización social”.
Belarra también ha animado a que “la gente se siga movilizando y organizando” y ha afirmado que la “única medida con un carácter mínimamente estructural”, en relación a la renovación automática de los alquileres, se incluye en un decreto que “el PSOE reconoce en privado que va a caer”.
Compromís lamenta que el Gobierno haya dividido en dos el ‘decreto Maricarmen’
Àgueda Micó, diputada de Compromís en el Grupo Mixto, ha afirmado este martes que “la primera decepción [sobre las medidas de vivienda] es que sean dos reales decretos y no uno”. La diputada ha indicado que a su partido “no le gustan” algunas medidas incluidas en los dos decretos aprobados por el Consejo de Ministros, como los beneficios que se le otorgarán a los caseros que bajen el precio del alquiler. “Hay que ver la letra pequeña”, ha destacado Micó en los pasillos del Congreso antes de ingresar al pleno.
Rodríguez lamenta que en vivienda “el PP ni está ni se le espera”
La ministra de Vivienda, Isabel Rodríguez, ha lamentado que el PP “ni está ni se le espera” en el problema de la vivienda, “el principal problema de los españoles”. En la rueda de prensa del Consejo de Ministros, ha destacado que los periodistas no le hayan planteado ninguna pregunta sobre el partido liderado por Alberto Núñez Feijóo. “Lamento es que en una situación como esta el principal partido de la oposición n

deduped_items.body_text:
Una de cada cuatro españolas de 30 años sin hijos no los tiene porque se siente «demasiado joven»
Aumenta el número de mujeres que no quiere descendencia hasta el 15,5%
Hay un desacoplamiento evidente entre biología y percepción social. Hoy las españolas menores de 25 años sin hijos alegan como principal motivo para no tener descendencia que son «demasiado jóvenes» (41,5%). Desde entonces y hasta llegar a las puertas de los 30, una de ... cada cuatro sigue pensando lo mismo (26,5%) a pesar de que son los grupos de edad con las mejores condiciones biológicas para tener descendencia. Concuerda con los datos ya conocidos de natalidad: en España el primer hijo llega, de media, a los 31,5 años. Hace tres décadas, era a los 28,1.
Son algunos de los datos que arroja el avance de la Encuesta de Fecundidad de 2025 del Instituto Nacional de Estadística publicada este martes, que continúa la serie de trabajos llevados a cabo en 1977, 1985, 1999 y 2018. Su principal objetivo es identificar si las mujeres tienen más o menos hijos que los que desean y los motivos que pueden estar detrás de esa diferencia, como pueden ser los ingresos, la conciliación entre la vida familiar y laboral, la existencia de ayudas o la vida en pareja.
España vive una crisis en la natalidad. Las últimas cifras conocidas, de 2024, sitúan la media en 1,1 hijos por mujer, muy lejos de la tasa de remplazo de 2,1. Sin embargo, la mayor parte de las mujeres en España siguen queriendo tener hijos, según la encuesta publicada este martes. Hasta el 69,0% de las mujeres de 18 a 55 años deseaba tener al menos dos hijos en 2025. Esta expectativa, eso sí, está en descenso: en 2018, eran el 73,6%. En paralelo, crece también la cifra de aquellas que aseguran no querer ninguno: ahora son el 15,5% frente al 12,3% que constaban siete años atrás.
La realidad de un tercio de aquellas que sí quieren ser madres es que tienen menos hijos de los deseados, una cifra que asciende al 37,1% solo entre las españolas. Este dato se mantiene estable frente a 2018 (solo cinco décimas menos). A nivel global, el motivo principal que aducen es laboral, de conciliación y económico (28,5% entre las españolas), pero la lectura cambia radicalmente al desagregar la estadística por tramos de edad.
Margen de tiempo
Para las más jóvenes, es decir, aquellas que están en la edad idónea para tener hijos, la percepción es que aún hay tiempo. De hecho, hasta el 48,5% de las mujeres por debajo de los 30 dice que «todavía espera tener más hijos», un argumento que sigue siendo el principal (así lo apunta el 43,3%) en aquellas entre los 31 y los 34. Solo a partir de los 35, cuando también se desploma la fecundidad, empiezan a pesar más los motivos laborales, de conciliación y económicos y se convierte en el principal argumento esgrimido para no ampliar la familia. A pesar de todo, una de cada cuatro encuestadas a esta edad seguía pensando en ampliar la familia. Y esto es clave.
«La verdadera mentira no es que todo el mundo pueda tener hijos, sino que tenemos tiempo de sobra para tomar esa decisión más adelante», alegaba en un reciente artículo el conocido demógrafo británico Stephen J. Shaw en 'The Critic'. Porque esa percepción no es exclusiva de España. El experto se refería a los datos de un informe de la ONU publicado este año que reveló que, a nivel global, más del 70% de las mujeres de 35 a 39 años sin hijos aún deseaban tenerlos. En el caso de los hombres, el porcentaje llegaba a casi el 80%. Shaw apunta a que la presión social para que los jóvenes completen su educación y se labren una carrera «bajo la premisa de que aún habrá tiempo para encontrar pareja y formar una familia antes de que la curva de vitalidad se reduzca» es donde reside la verdadera mentira de la natalidad.
«No podemos elegir ser padres. Podemos soñar con serlo. Lo mínimo que podemos hacer es informar a la gente de lo rápido que cambian las probabilidades de que esa esperanza se cumpla», argumentaba.

Desde entonces y hasta llegar a las puertas de los 30, una de ... cada cuatro sigue pensando lo mismo (26,5%) a pesar de que son los grupos de edad con las mejores condiciones biológicas para tener descendencia. Concuerda con los datos ya conocidos de natalidad: en España el primer hijo llega, de media, a los 31,5 años. Hace tres décadas, era a los 28,1.
Son algunos de los datos que arroja el avance de la Encuesta de Fecundidad de 2025 del Instituto Nacional de Estadística publicada este martes, que continúa la serie de trabajos llevados a cabo en 1977, 1985, 1999 y 2018. Su principal objetivo es identificar si las mujeres tienen más o menos hijos que los que desean y los motivos que pueden estar detrás de esa diferencia, como pueden ser los ingresos, la conciliación entre la vida familiar y laboral, la existencia de ayudas o la vida en pareja.
España vive una crisis en la natalidad. Las últimas cifras conocidas, de 2024, sitúan la media en 1,1 hijos por mujer, muy lejos de la tasa de remplazo de 2,1. Sin embargo, la mayor parte de las mujeres en España siguen queriendo tener hijos, según la encuesta publicada este martes. Hasta el 69,0% de las mujeres de 18 a 55 años deseaba tener al menos dos hijos en 2025. Esta expectativa, eso sí, está en descenso: en 2018, eran el 73,6%. En paralelo, crece también la cifra de aquellas que aseguran no querer ninguno: ahora son el 15,5% frente al 12,3% que constaban siete años atrás.
La realidad de un tercio de aquellas que sí quieren ser madres es que tienen menos hijos de los deseados, una cifra que asciende al 37,1% solo entre las españolas. Este dato se mantiene estable frente a 2018 (solo cinco décimas menos). A nivel global, el motivo principal que aducen es laboral, de conciliación y económico (28,5% entre las españolas), pero la lectura cambia radicalmente al desagregar la estadística por tramos de edad.
Margen de tiempo
Para las más jóvenes, es decir, aquellas que están en la edad idónea para tener hijos, la percepción es que aún hay tiempo. De hecho, hasta el 48,5% de las mujeres por debajo de los 30 dice que «todavía espera tener más hijos», un argumento que sigue siendo el principal (así lo apunta el 43,3%) en aquellas entre los 31 y los 34. Solo a partir de los 35, cuando también se desploma la fecundidad, empiezan a pesar más los motivos laborales, de conciliación y económicos y se convierte en el principal argumento esgrimido para no ampliar la familia. A pesar de todo, una de cada cuatro encuestadas a esta edad seguía pensando en ampliar la familia. Y esto es clave.
«La verdadera mentira no es que todo el mundo pueda tener hijos, sino que tenemos tiempo de sobra para tomar esa decisión más adelante», alegaba en un reciente artículo el conocido demógrafo británico Stephen J. Shaw en 'The Critic'. Porque esa percepción no es exclusiva de España. El experto se refería a los datos de un informe de la ONU publicado este año que reveló que, a nivel global, más del 70% de las mujeres de 35 a 39 años sin hijos aún deseaban tenerlos. En el caso de los hombres, el porcentaje llegaba a casi el 80%. Shaw apunta a que la presión social para que los jóvenes completen su educación y se labren una carrera «bajo la premisa de que aún habrá tiempo para encontrar pareja y formar una familia antes de que la curva de vitalidad se reduzca» es donde reside la verdadera mentira de la natalidad.
«No podemos elegir ser padres. Podemos soñar con serlo. Lo mínimo que podemos hacer es informar a la gente de lo rápido que cambian las probabilidades de que esa esperanza se cumpla», argumentaba.

deduped_items.title: Supreme Court upholds Covid consipracy theorist's conviction of incitement
deduped_items.summary: The Supreme Court upheld the conviction of conspiracy theorist Willem Engel of Viruswaarheid, sentencing him to 60 hours of community service for incitement during the coronavirus pandemi
deduped_items.body_text:
Supreme Court upholds Covid consipracy theorist's conviction of incitement
The Supreme Court upheld the conviction of conspiracy theorist Willem Engel of Viruswaarheid, sentencing him to 60 hours of community service for incitement during the coronavirus pandemic. No further appeal is possible against this ruling, made on Tuesday.
In June 2020, Viruswaarheid wanted to hold a protest on the Malieveld in The Hague, but the municipality had banned it due to the coronavirus-related restrictions at the time and a previous protest that ended in violence. Engel then held a livestream on social media, saying that he would still protest on the Malieveld in his own capacity, and inviting “everyone to come.”
The demonstration ultimately ended in a violent confrontation with the police.
In March 2025, the Court of Appeal convicted Engel of incitement and sentenced him to 60 hours of community service. The Supreme Court now rejected Engel’s appeal against that ruling.
According to the Supreme Court, the Appeals Court correctly ruled that Engel was actively inciting people to commit a crime - participating in a banned demonstration - with his live stream in June 2020. The Appeals Court acknowledged that this was an infringement on the rights to freedom of expression and freedom of assembly, but held that this was necessary given the public health crisis ongoing at the time.
The Appeals Court also rightly ruled that Engel’s statements could “by no means” be construed as calls for a peaceful protest. He made this call against the backdrop of a previous Viruswaarheid protest that ended in a violent clash with the police. And his call included the statements: “It cannot be stopped. The resistance group is likely arriving with 500 tractors, so don’t worry. We will open up the highways if necessary.” He also spoke of acting “in love and patience, naturally non-violent and non-cooperation.” But the Supreme Court confirmed the ruling that, when viewed as a whole, his statements cannot be considered a call for peaceful protest.
“The Supreme Court dismisses the appeal.”
The Supreme Court’s ruling deviates from the advice given by the Advocate General. In February, the Advocate General had recommended a partial retrial, arguing that the Court of Appeal did not sufficiently justify why criminal prosecution was necessary.

deduped_items.title: Supreme Court upholds Covid consipracy theorist's conviction of incitement
deduped_items.summary: The Supreme Court upheld the conviction of conspiracy theorist Willem Engel of Viruswaarheid, sentencing him to 60 hours of community service for incitement during the coronavirus pandemi
deduped_items.body_text:
Supreme Court upholds Covid consipracy theorist's conviction of incitement
The Supreme Court upheld the conviction of conspiracy theorist Willem Engel of Viruswaarheid, sentencing him to 60 hours of community service for incitement during the coronavirus pandemic. No further appeal is possible against this ruling, made on Tuesday.
In June 2020, Viruswaarheid wanted to hold a protest on the Malieveld in The Hague, but the municipality had banned it due to the coronavirus-related restrictions at the time and a previous protest that ended in violence. Engel then held a livestream on social media, saying that he would still protest on the Malieveld in his own capacity, and inviting “everyone to come.”
The demonstration ultimately ended in a violent confrontation with the police.
In March 2025, the Court of Appeal convicted Engel of incitement and sentenced him to 60 hours of community service. The Supreme Court now rejected Engel’s appeal against that ruling.
According to the Supreme Court, the Appeals Court correctly ruled that Engel was actively inciting people to commit a crime - participating in a banned demonstration - with his live stream in June 2020. The Appeals Court acknowledged that this was an infringement on the rights to freedom of expression and freedom of assembly, but held that this was necessary given the public health crisis ongoing at the time.
The Appeals Court also rightly ruled that Engel’s statements could “by no means” be construed as calls for a peaceful protest. He made this call against the backdrop of a previous Viruswaarheid protest that ended in a violent clash with the police. And his call included the statements: “It cannot be stopped. The resistance group is likely arriving with 500 tractors, so don’t worry. We will open up the highways if necessary.” He also spoke of acting “in love and patience, naturally non-violent and non-cooperation.” But the Supreme Court confirmed the ruling that, when viewed as a whole, his statements cannot be considered a call for peaceful protest.
“The Supreme Court dismisses the appeal.”
The Supreme Court’s ruling deviates from the advice given by the Advocate General. In February, the Advocate General had recommended a partial retrial, arguing that the Court of Appeal did not sufficiently justify why criminal prosecution was necessary.

deduped_items.title: 2,200 Hungarian Students Begin Studies at Babes-Bolyai University in Romania
deduped_items.summary: More than 16,000 freshmen are beginning their higher education studies this year at Babes-Bolyai University (BBTE) in Cluj-Napoca (Kolozsvár), of whom nearly 2,200 are enrolled in Hungarian-language programs, Maszol.ro reported on Monday. Among the students enrolled in Hungarian-language programs, 1,579 are studying in full-time or distance-learning undergraduate programs, while 577 are beginning master’s programs. In […] The post 2,200 Hungarian Students Begin Studies at Babes-Bolyai University
deduped_items.body_text:
The more than HUF 4 billion project included campus renovations and new digital equipment.Continue reading
More than 16,000 freshmen are beginning their higher education studies this year at Babes-Bolyai University (BBTE) in Cluj-Napoca (Kolozsvár), of whom nearly 2,200 are enrolled in Hungarian-language programs, Maszol.ro reported on Monday.
Among the students enrolled in Hungarian-language programs, 1,579 are studying in full-time or distance-learning undergraduate programs, while 577 are beginning master’s programs. In the bachelor’s program, 46 percent of first-year students enrolled in tuition-based spots, while in the master’s program, approximately 30 percent of students were admitted to tuition-based spots.
At the university’s opening ceremony, Rector Daniel David emphasized that BBTE is one of Eastern Europe’s most significant centers of higher education and its most complex multicultural institution. He pointed out that,
reflecting the history of Transylvania and the institution, Hungarian and German are considered official languages at the university alongside Romanian.
According to the rector, BBTE’s identity is built on the importance of science, culture, and innovation. Daniel David described the university as a “bastion of scientific truth and democracy” in an era in which pseudosciences and anti-democratic movements pose a serious challenge to society.
Bálint Markó, the vice rector responsible for the Hungarian division, emphasized that, in light of the PISA results, the university must simultaneously respond constructively to shortcomings and preserve intellectual freedom in order to launch new, forward-looking programs. He stated that the educational institution must strive to respond to societal needs, while at the same time holding fast to certain programs that it must not abandon, even if they seem unnecessary.
We must be free in our thoughts and initiatives, and we must pass this on to our students and to society. These must be the guiding principles for the university and for the operation and development of the Hungarian department,”
Maszol quoted the vice rector as saying in his speech delivered in Hungarian.
According to information from the university’s communications office, the dual-major programs launched last year have lived up to expectations. A sufficient number of applicants were admitted to the Hungarian Language and Literature–Folklore, Mathematics–Computer Science, Physics–Computer Science, and Philosophy–Art History programs, meaning that classes will begin this fall for all dual-major programs.
Starting this academic year, the Hungarian-language undergraduate program in Public Administration will resume in a distance learning format at the BBTE’s branch campus in Sfantu-Gheorghe (Sepsiszentgyörgy); this program attracted significant interest during the fall admissions cycle, with nearly twice as many applicants as available spots.
This summer, BBTE obtained the necessary permits to launch a doctoral program in medicine. The doctoral program will begin in the fall of 2026, and prospective doctoral students will have the opportunity to work with a Hungarian-speaking doctoral advisor, the university announced.
Via MTI, Maszol.ro; Featured photo: Yerpo / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

deduped_items.body_text:
Czech Study Finds Supporting Homeless People Can Save Public Money
Prague Morning
A Czech experiment in which homeless people received CZK 100,000 with no conditions attached suggests that early financial support can reduce some of the costs associated with homelessness.
The project, known as New Leaf, was carried out by the Czech organization Neposeda in cooperation with researchers from Charles University.
The findings indicate that the state spends an average of about CZK 200,000 a year on each person experiencing homelessness, with healthcare, social services and police work accounting for a significant share of the total.
The researchers concluded that leaving people without support can ultimately be more expensive for public finances than providing targeted assistance.
How the New Leaf experiment worked
The project ran from summer 2024 until the end of 2025 and was inspired by a similar initiative in Canada.
Researchers focused on people who had been living on the streets for no more than two and a half years. The aim was to examine whether intervention at an earlier stage of homelessness could prevent longer-term problems.
Participants were divided into several groups. Forty people received CZK 100,000 without restrictions on how the money could be used. Another 20 were offered the support of a personal social worker instead, while 40 people formed a control group and received no additional assistance.
The study initially involved 100 people. One participant died from a serious illness shortly after the project began, leaving 99 participants in the final research sample.
The researchers tracked participants’ use of public services and their contact with state authorities, including emergency medical services, hospitals, outpatient healthcare, social services and police.
Healthcare accounts for the largest share
The study estimates that the state spends around CZK 200,000 annually on each homeless person.
Healthcare represented almost 43% of the estimated expenditure. Low-threshold services, which provide basic support and a safe place for people experiencing homelessness, accounted for around a quarter of the total.
Police work represented another 9%, or more than 18,000 crowns per person each year.
The wider cost to public finances
Data from the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs recorded 11,641 homeless people in the Czech Republic in the previous year.
Based on the estimated annual cost per person, direct public expenditure associated with homelessness amounts to roughly 2.33 billion crowns a year.

deduped_items.body_text:
Home Baking Returns to Czech Kitchens as Flour Sales Rise
Prague Morning
Home baking is gaining momentum in the Czech Republic, with online supermarket Rohlik.cz reporting a sharp increase in demand for baking ingredients this year.
Flour has been at the center of the trend. Sales of organic flour have risen by almost 72 percent compared with the previous year, while conventional flour sales increased by around 23 percent.
The change has also affected the balance of sales. Organic flour previously accounted for about 19 percent of flour purchases at Rohlik.cz. That figure has now climbed to almost 25 percent.
The figures suggest that customers are not simply buying more flour but are also paying greater attention to the type and quality of the ingredients they use.
Rohlik.cz CEO Miroslava Vopatová says baking continues to play a role in family life, particularly as an activity shared across generations. The supermarket has responded by offering products at different price points, from private-label options to organic and farm-produced ingredients.
Yeast sales tell a different story
The increase in demand for flour has not been mirrored by yeast.
Sales of yeast have been gradually falling since the surge in home baking during the coronavirus pandemic. One shift remains noticeable, however: shoppers are increasingly choosing fresh yeast rather than dried yeast.
Home baking in the Czech Republic is also strongly seasonal. Christmas remains the busiest period of the year, while a smaller increase usually occurs in March and April. Demand drops during the summer months.
For experienced bakers, the quality of the final product often depends on relatively simple details. Yeast dough needs enough time and warmth to rise properly, while rushing the process can affect the result.
The preparation of the filling matters as well. Curd cheese should be drained thoroughly before being added to a cake or pastry, reducing the risk of excess moisture making the dough soggy. Fruit fillings should also be sufficiently thick rather than watery.
These practical details can make a noticeable difference, particularly in traditional Czech pastries whose recipes are often passed down through families.

deduped_items.title: Govt targets drug inmate rehab to ease prison overcrowding
deduped_items.summary: President Prabowo Subianto has instructed Law Minister Supratman Andi Agtas to formulate a comprehensive rehabilitation ...
deduped_items.body_text:
"I was specifically asked to coordinate with several ministries and agencies—including the Head of the National Narcotics Agency (BNN), the Head of the National Research and Innovation Agency (BRIN), and other ministers—to devise a rehabilitation plan targeting drug users inside correctional facilities," Supratman said after a limited cabinet meeting at the Presidential Palace Complex in Jakarta on Tuesday.
The directive comes in response to severe overcrowding across the national prison network.
Data from the Directorate General of Corrections as of April 2026 shows that prisons and detention centers nationwide house over 271,000 inmates against a capacity of approximately 146,000, resulting in an overcrowding rate of about 85 percent.
Official records as of May 4, 2026, indicate that 146,284 inmates, or 53.9 percent of the national prison population, are incarcerated for narcotics-related offenses.
BNN Head Suyudi Ario Seto noted that his agency will work closely with relevant ministries to define the criteria and mechanisms for providing medical and social rehabilitation to incarcerated users.
"We will hold a more in-depth coordination meeting regarding rehabilitation efforts, specifically concerning users or inmates involved in narcotics cases who have been processed and detained but still require rehabilitation," Suyudi stated.
In addition to prison reform, Minister Supratman reported to the President progress on legal aid accessibility, highlighting the establishment of roughly 83,960 community legal aid posts (posbankum) across villages and urban communities nationwide.
Out of approximately 16,000 complaints received by these posts, around 14,000 cases were resolved through mediation using a restorative justice approach, while the remaining two thousand are receiving free legal aid services.

deduped_items.title: Govt targets drug inmate rehab to ease prison overcrowding
deduped_items.summary: President Prabowo Subianto has instructed Law Minister Supratman Andi Agtas to formulate a comprehensive rehabilitation ...
deduped_items.body_text:
"I was specifically asked to coordinate with several ministries and agencies—including the Head of the National Narcotics Agency (BNN), the Head of the National Research and Innovation Agency (BRIN), and other ministers—to devise a rehabilitation plan targeting drug users inside correctional facilities," Supratman said after a limited cabinet meeting at the Presidential Palace Complex in Jakarta on Tuesday.
The directive comes in response to severe overcrowding across the national prison network.
Data from the Directorate General of Corrections as of April 2026 shows that prisons and detention centers nationwide house over 271,000 inmates against a capacity of approximately 146,000, resulting in an overcrowding rate of about 85 percent.
Official records as of May 4, 2026, indicate that 146,284 inmates, or 53.9 percent of the national prison population, are incarcerated for narcotics-related offenses.
BNN Head Suyudi Ario Seto noted that his agency will work closely with relevant ministries to define the criteria and mechanisms for providing medical and social rehabilitation to incarcerated users.
"We will hold a more in-depth coordination meeting regarding rehabilitation efforts, specifically concerning users or inmates involved in narcotics cases who have been processed and detained but still require rehabilitation," Suyudi stated.
In addition to prison reform, Minister Supratman reported to the President progress on legal aid accessibility, highlighting the establishment of roughly 83,960 community legal aid posts (posbankum) across villages and urban communities nationwide.
Out of approximately 16,000 complaints received by these posts, around 14,000 cases were resolved through mediation using a restorative justice approach, while the remaining two thousand are receiving free legal aid services.

Data from the Directorate General of Corrections as of April 2026 shows that prisons and detention centers nationwide house over 271,000 inmates against a capacity of approximately 146,000, resulting in an overcrowding rate of about 85 percent.
Official records as of May 4, 2026, indicate that 146,284 inmates, or 53.9 percent of the national prison population, are incarcerated for narcotics-related offenses.
BNN Head Suyudi Ario Seto noted that his agency will work closely with relevant ministries to define the criteria and mechanisms for providing medical and social rehabilitation to incarcerated users.
"We will hold a more in-depth coordination meeting regarding rehabilitation efforts, specifically concerning users or inmates involved in narcotics cases who have been processed and detained but still require rehabilitation," Suyudi stated.
In addition to prison reform, Minister Supratman reported to the President progress on legal aid accessibility, highlighting the establishment of roughly 83,960 community legal aid posts (posbankum) across villages and urban communities nationwide.
Out of approximately 16,000 complaints received by these posts, around 14,000 cases were resolved through mediation using a restorative justice approach, while the remaining two thousand are receiving free legal aid services.

deduped_items.title: Thai students spared from Australia's ban on bringing family members
deduped_items.summary: Thai students will not be affected by Australia's latest visa restrictions banning most international students from bringing family members with them, Australian authorities have confirmed, as Canberra seeks to deepen cooperation with Thailand in trade, migration and regional security.
deduped_items.body_text:
Matt Thistlethwaite, Australia's Assistant Minister for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Assistant Minister for Immigration, made the announcement last week during a two-day official visit to Thailand.
Speaking in Bangkok on Sept. 23, Thistlethwaite said Thailand had been excluded from several new migration restrictions because of the close ties between the two countries, the Bangkok Post reported.
He said Thai students would not be subject to the new restrictions, with Thailand among ASEAN and Pacific countries exempted from several of the measures.
"There's no restrictions on Thai people coming to study in Australia, bringing their family members as well. We're very welcoming of Thai students coming to Australia to study at our universities and technical colleges, and it's been a growing relationship that we're happy to foster into the future," he said, as seen in a transcript published on the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade's website.
"We're seeing more and more Thai students studying at Australian universities, and the Thai diaspora in Australia is about 80,000, and we have the third largest Thai diaspora of any country in the world, and that's something that Australia is very, very proud of, and we want to encourage more of, and the Free Trade Agreement helps us to do that," he said.
Australia recently introduced tightening rules for international students.
Australian Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke announced on Sept. 17 new measures that will limit accompanying family members for most student and post-study work visa holders, crack down on "visa hopping" by tightening rules on switching courses and visa types to extend stays, apply "No Further Stay" conditions to visitor visas, and prioritize visa applications for skilled workers in industries with labor shortages.
The measures form part of Canberra's efforts to bring net overseas migration down from about 290,000 to 225,000 by 2027-28.
Vietnamese students may also be spared from the new restrictions
Brian Quang Dinh, director of consultancy Edunetwork Australia, told Vietnam News Agency in Sydney the key message from the latest changes was that Australia still needs international students and skilled workers but wants to ensure temporary visas are used for their intended purposes.
He said Burke's announcement specified that ASEAN countries and Pacific island nations, along with certain groups of students such as PhD candidates, would be exempt from some of the new restrictions.
Vietnamese passport holders are currently among those allowed to continue bringing family members, subject to applicable conditions, he said.
The restrictions come after the hard-right One Nation party, which has been surging in recent polls, said it would slash the number of temporary migrants by 750,000 over three years to give Australians "breathing space," Reuters reported.
One Nation, which describes its approach as "Australia first" and whose policies have drawn comparisons to those of U.S. President Donald Trump, said it would aim to restrict net overseas migration to 130,000 after the initial three years, with the program expected to be reviewed annually.
Australia’s migration intake, driven largely by international students, backpackers and temporary skilled workers, surged after the country reopened its borders in February 2022 following nearly two years of Covid-19 restrictions, according to Reuters.

Matt Thistlethwaite, Australia's Assistant Minister for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Assistant Minister for Immigration, made the announcement last week during a two-day official visit to Thailand.
Speaking in Bangkok on Sept. 23, Thistlethwaite said Thailand had been excluded from several new migration restrictions because of the close ties between the two countries, the Bangkok Post reported.
He said Thai students would not be subject to the new restrictions, with Thailand among ASEAN and Pacific countries exempted from several of the measures.
"There's no restrictions on Thai people coming to study in Australia, bringing their family members as well. We're very welcoming of Thai students coming to Australia to study at our universities and technical colleges, and it's been a growing relationship that we're happy to foster into the future," he said, as seen in a transcript published on the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade's website.

He said Burke's announcement specified that ASEAN countries and Pacific island nations, along with certain groups of students such as PhD candidates, would be exempt from some of the new restrictions.

deduped_items.summary: Thai students will not be affected by Australia's latest visa restrictions banning most international students from bringing family members with them, Australian authorities have confirmed, as Canberra seeks to deepen cooperation with Thailand in trade, migration and regional security.
deduped_items.body_text:
Matt Thistlethwaite, Australia's Assistant Minister for Foreign Affairs and Trade and Assistant Minister for Immigration, made the announcement last week during a two-day official visit to Thailand.
Speaking in Bangkok on Sept. 23, Thistlethwaite said Thailand had been excluded from several new migration restrictions because of the close ties between the two countries, the Bangkok Post reported.
He said Thai students would not be subject to the new restrictions, with Thailand among ASEAN and Pacific countries exempted from several of the measures.
"There's no restrictions on Thai people coming to study in Australia, bringing their family members as well. We're very welcoming of Thai students coming to Australia to study at our universities and technical colleges, and it's been a growing relationship that we're happy to foster into the future," he said, as seen in a transcript published on the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade's website.
"We're seeing more and more Thai students studying at Australian universities, and the Thai diaspora in Australia is about 80,000, and we have the third largest Thai diaspora of any country in the world, and that's something that Australia is very, very proud of, and we want to encourage more of, and the Free Trade Agreement helps us to do that," he said.
Australia recently introduced tightening rules for international students.
Australian Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke announced on Sept. 17 new measures that will limit accompanying family members for most student and post-study work visa holders, crack down on "visa hopping" by tightening rules on switching courses and visa types to extend stays, apply "No Further Stay" conditions to visitor visas, and prioritize visa applications for skilled workers in industries with labor shortages.
The measures form part of Canberra's efforts to bring net overseas migration down from about 290,000 to 225,000 by 2027-28.
Vietnamese students may also be spared from the new restrictions
Brian Quang Dinh, director of consultancy Edunetwork Australia, told Vietnam News Agency in Sydney the key message from the latest changes was that Australia still needs international students and skilled workers but wants to ensure temporary visas are used for their intended purposes.
He said Burke's announcement specified that ASEAN countries and Pacific island nations, along with certain groups of students such as PhD candidates, would be exempt from some of the new restrictions.
Vietnamese passport holders are currently among those allowed to continue bringing family members, subject to applicable conditions, he said.
The restrictions come after the hard-right One Nation party, which has been surging in recent polls, said it would slash the number of temporary migrants by 750,000 over three years to give Australians "breathing space," Reuters reported.
One Nation, which describes its approach as "Australia first" and whose policies have drawn comparisons to those of U.S. President Donald Trump, said it would aim to restrict net overseas migration to 130,000 after the initial three years, with the program expected to be reviewed annually.
Australia’s migration intake, driven largely by international students, backpackers and temporary skilled workers, surged after the country reopened its borders in February 2022 following nearly two years of Covid-19 restrictions, according to Reuters.

Speaking in Bangkok on Sept. 23, Thistlethwaite said Thailand had been excluded from several new migration restrictions because of the close ties between the two countries, the Bangkok Post reported.
He said Thai students would not be subject to the new restrictions, with Thailand among ASEAN and Pacific countries exempted from several of the measures.
"There's no restrictions on Thai people coming to study in Australia, bringing their family members as well. We're very welcoming of Thai students coming to Australia to study at our universities and technical colleges, and it's been a growing relationship that we're happy to foster into the future," he said, as seen in a transcript published on the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade's website.
"We're seeing more and more Thai students studying at Australian universities, and the Thai diaspora in Australia is about 80,000, and we have the third largest Thai diaspora of any country in the world, and that's something that Australia is very, very proud of, and we want to encourage more of, and the Free Trade Agreement helps us to do that," he said.
Australia recently introduced tightening rules for international students.
Australian Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke announced on Sept. 17 new measures that will limit accompanying family members for most student and post-study work visa holders, crack down on "visa hopping" by tightening rules on switching courses and visa types to extend stays, apply "No Further Stay" conditions to visitor visas, and prioritize visa applications for skilled workers in industries with labor shortages.
The measures form part of Canberra's efforts to bring net overseas migration down from about 290,000 to 225,000 by 2027-28.
Vietnamese students may also be spared from the new restrictions
Brian Quang Dinh, director of consultancy Edunetwork Australia, told Vietnam News Agency in Sydney the key message from the latest changes was that Australia still needs international students and skilled workers but wants to ensure temporary visas are used for their intended purposes.
He said Burke's announcement specified that ASEAN countries and Pacific island nations, along with certain groups of students such as PhD candidates, would be exempt from some of the new restrictions.
Vietnamese passport holders are currently among those allowed to continue bringing family members, subject to applicable conditions, he said.
The restrictions come after the hard-right One Nation party, which has been surging in recent polls, said it would slash the number of temporary migrants by 750,000 over three years to give Australians "breathing space," Reuters reported.
One Nation, which describes its approach as "Australia first" and whose policies have drawn comparisons to those of U.S. President Donald Trump, said it would aim to restrict net overseas migration to 130,000 after the initial three years, with the program expected to be reviewed annually.
Australia’s migration intake, driven largely by international students, backpackers and temporary skilled workers, surged after the country reopened its borders in February 2022 following nearly two years of Covid-19 restrictions, according to Reuters.

deduped_items.title: 5,600 delayed bags, 330 stalled flights prompt THAI apology
deduped_items.summary: Thai Airways International’s (THAI) mishandling of passenger luggage and flight delays caused by flooding have severely damaged Thailand’s image and undermined confidence in its tourism sector, Tourism and Sports Minister Surasak Phancharoenworakul said on Tuesday.
deduped_items.body_text:
Thai Airways International’s (THAI) mishandling of passenger luggage and flight delays caused by flooding have severely damaged Thailand’s image and undermined confidence in its tourism sector, Tourism and Sports Minister Surasak Phancharoenworakul said on Tuesday.
Although flooding prevented some staff from commuting normally, the primary cause of the disruption was the airline’s lack of operational readiness and management preparedness, Mr Surasak said.
The minister added that he had personally encountered the problems while returning to Thailand from Japan on a Thai Airways flight.
Torrential rain and flooding in Bangkok over the weekend caused delays involving about 5,600 pieces of luggage and 330 Thai Airways flights, after hundreds of employees were stranded at home and unable to report to work at the country’s two main international airports, Suvarnabhumi and Don Mueang.
The flag carrier said on Tuesday that it aimed to clear the baggage backlog within three days. It had also ordered a 30% reduction in daily flights to allow operations to reset and improve punctuality. A compensation claim process has been opened for affected passengers.
Thai Airways chief apologises
Thai Airways chief executive Chai Eamsiri said the airline’s initial impact assessment had been inaccurate. Flooding prevented about 300 ground staff and specialised personnel from reporting to work, he said during a press conference, while apologising to passengers for the inconvenience.
The airline has about 500 ground staff but was short of 200 to 300 workers during the disruption. Its normal schedule of around 110 flights a day was cut by 30% to help manage the remaining flights and improve on-time performance after almost all flights were delayed, Mr Chai said.
Luggage piled up on the second floor of Suvarnabhumi airport’s passenger terminal after overflowing the conveyor belts on Tuesday. (Photo: Nutthawat Wichieanbut)
Mr Surasak said the problems may have stemmed from the airline assigning staff to serve other carriers under its ground-handling contracts to avoid contractual penalties. This, he said, resulted in the most severe delays affecting Thai Airways' own passengers.
He also criticised the airline for failing to take proactive action despite receiving offers of assistance from several agencies. The national carrier did not provide food or accommodation for military personnel deployed by the Defence Ministry to help clear the baggage backlog, forcing the soldiers to return to their units for meals.
"Every agency tried to step in and help, yet there was no positive response or cooperation from Thai Airways," Mr Surasak said. "I believe Thai Airways executives need to adopt a more proactive approach.
If they feel their term is ending and are unwilling to resolve these issues, they should consider resigning so that others who are truly committed can step in to manage the situation."
Thai Airways brought in three other delivery providers, including Thailand Post and its existing service provider, to help distribute baggage. Airports of Thailand (AOT) assisted with space allocation, while the Royal Thai Air Force, the Defence Ministry and Thai Airways’ headquarters staff provided additional personnel.
Chai: Initial assessment had not been accurate
Deputy Transport Minister Siripong Angkasakulkiat issued a blunt warning.
“If Thai Airways chooses not to look after its passengers, the business repercussions and damage will ultimately rebound on the company itself,” he said.

deduped_items.title: ‘If we can’t sell oil, no one else will’: Iran threatens regional infrastructure as Hormuz talks stall
deduped_items.summary: TEHRAN, Sept 29 — Iran today threatened to attack infrastructure around the Middle East, intensifying its rhetoric...
deduped_items.body_text:
TEHRAN, Sept 29 — Iran today threatened to attack infrastructure around the Middle East, intensifying its rhetoric as it awaits a formal response from Washington on a new plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
US President Donald Trump has already dismissed the proposal from Tehran, but Iran’s foreign minister said yesterday that he was expecting a formal response from American officials in the coming day.
Fighting has subsided in recent weeks, though Tehran has continued to target ships in the strait, with Washington falling back on an economic pressure campaign instead of further military action.
Iran’s chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf today threatened new attacks, saying no infrastructure in the region would be safe if his country’s security was not guaranteed.
“In a region where we cannot sell oil, no one else will sell oil either; or if our security is not guaranteed, no infrastructure will remain safe,” Ghalibaf, who is also Iran’s parliament speaker, said according to video released by state TV.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said he expected a formal answer from the US today to Tehran’s proposal, state media reported.
Iran has maintained a blockade on commercial shipping through Hormuz since the war began in late February with US-Israeli strikes on the Islamic republic.
The shipping route carried a fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas before the conflict began.
The US military has been maintaining a counterblockade of Iran’s ports in an effort to prevent Tehran from exporting oil.
Conditions
Araghchi said late yesterday that Qatari intermediaries “presented ideas, and we discussed them; they are set to raise the matter with the American side once more, after which the final US response will be conveyed to us”.
The top diplomat, who was in New York for the UN General Assembly, said “the Qataris hope this will be done by tomorrow”.
“The current focus is solely on the Strait of Hormuz, and the reopening of the strait is contingent upon the fulfilment of certain conditions that we have communicated to the other side,” he added.
Last week, discussions were held in New York between Araghchi and US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
As a precondition for ending its blockade, Iran is demanding a seven-day ceasefire across the Middle East, including in Lebanon, where its ally Hezbollah is regularly bombarded by Israel.
It is also demanding the unfreezing of Iranian assets abroad, the lifting of sanctions on its oil sector and an end to the US naval blockade on its ports.
Both sides claim to have control of Hormuz, with the US saying oil is moving through and Tehran insisting the waterway is closed.
Today, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, the ideological arm of the country’s military, said “the US claim that it remains open is false”.
“Sneaking a few hundred barrels of oil through under the cover of darkness — with transponders turned off and at great cost — does not constitute the strait being open,” said spokesperson Hossein Mohebi.
“A truly open strait is one where, as in the past, at least 125 vessels would pass through daily, transporting a minimum of 20 million barrels of oil and petroleum products.
“Any vessel attempting to pass through sustains damage — either we strike it, or it hits a mine,” he added. — AFP

deduped_items.title: ‘If we can’t sell oil, no one else will’: Iran threatens regional infrastructure as Hormuz talks stall
deduped_items.summary: TEHRAN, Sept 29 — Iran today threatened to attack infrastructure around the Middle East, intensifying its rhetoric...
deduped_items.body_text:
TEHRAN, Sept 29 — Iran today threatened to attack infrastructure around the Middle East, intensifying its rhetoric as it awaits a formal response from Washington on a new plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
US President Donald Trump has already dismissed the proposal from Tehran, but Iran’s foreign minister said yesterday that he was expecting a formal response from American officials in the coming day.
Fighting has subsided in recent weeks, though Tehran has continued to target ships in the strait, with Washington falling back on an economic pressure campaign instead of further military action.
Iran’s chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf today threatened new attacks, saying no infrastructure in the region would be safe if his country’s security was not guaranteed.
“In a region where we cannot sell oil, no one else will sell oil either; or if our security is not guaranteed, no infrastructure will remain safe,” Ghalibaf, who is also Iran’s parliament speaker, said according to video released by state TV.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said he expected a formal answer from the US today to Tehran’s proposal, state media reported.
Iran has maintained a blockade on commercial shipping through Hormuz since the war began in late February with US-Israeli strikes on the Islamic republic.
The shipping route carried a fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas before the conflict began.
The US military has been maintaining a counterblockade of Iran’s ports in an effort to prevent Tehran from exporting oil.
Conditions
Araghchi said late yesterday that Qatari intermediaries “presented ideas, and we discussed them; they are set to raise the matter with the American side once more, after which the final US response will be conveyed to us”.
The top diplomat, who was in New York for the UN General Assembly, said “the Qataris hope this will be done by tomorrow”.
“The current focus is solely on the Strait of Hormuz, and the reopening of the strait is contingent upon the fulfilment of certain conditions that we have communicated to the other side,” he added.
Last week, discussions were held in New York between Araghchi and US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
As a precondition for ending its blockade, Iran is demanding a seven-day ceasefire across the Middle East, including in Lebanon, where its ally Hezbollah is regularly bombarded by Israel.
It is also demanding the unfreezing of Iranian assets abroad, the lifting of sanctions on its oil sector and an end to the US naval blockade on its ports.
Both sides claim to have control of Hormuz, with the US saying oil is moving through and Tehran insisting the waterway is closed.
Today, Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, the ideological arm of the country’s military, said “the US claim that it remains open is false”.
“Sneaking a few hundred barrels of oil through under the cover of darkness — with transponders turned off and at great cost — does not constitute the strait being open,” said spokesperson Hossein Mohebi.
“A truly open strait is one where, as in the past, at least 125 vessels would pass through daily, transporting a minimum of 20 million barrels of oil and petroleum products.
“Any vessel attempting to pass through sustains damage — either we strike it, or it hits a mine,” he added. — AFP

deduped_items.summary: An estimated 645 million people worldwide face hunger. When disruptions occur, they reverberate far beyond an immediate conflict zone. While everyone is affected, the most vulnerable countries, communities and persons are least able to absorb another shock to food prices and supplies.

deduped_items.body_text:
ISLAMABAD: Opposition alliance Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) on Tuesday invited the PPP, a key ally of the ruling PML-N in the Centre, to attend multiparty conference that is being planned by the opposition.
For its part, the PPP said it “welcomes the move” and would forward the invitation to the party’s chairperson, Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari. The TTAP would then be informed of his stance.
The development was confirmed in separate but similar statements by the two sides.
The opposition had first announced its intention to hold a multiparty moot on Sept 11, with the PTI leading the initiative. PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan had outlined plans to hold the conference, saying that “the current law and order situation, the economy, inflation, lawlessness, and the creation of new provinces issue” called for such measures.
His statement to the media came after a meeting with Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) leaders, who have agreed to attend the opposition’s moot.
A delegation of the TTAP, led by Barrister Gohar, called on PPP Secretary General Nayyar Hussain Bukhari at the party’s Central Secretariat in Islamabad and formally invited his party to the moot as well, statements by the two sides said.
The delegation also included Leader of Opposition in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, Senator Zeeshan Akhunzada and TTAP spokesperson Akhunzada Hussain Yousafzai.
The TTAP delegation briefed Bukhari on the objectives and purpose of the planned multiparty conference, the statements said.
They also discussed the political situation in the country, supremacy of the Constitution, strengthening of democratic institutions, contacts between political parties and other matters.
The statements quoted Bukhari as saying that the PPP considered “engagement and consultation with political parties on constitutional and democratic matters important”.
Speaking to Dawn after the meeting, TTAP spokesperson Yousafzai said the multiparty conference would be held after PTI’s protest, which is scheduled for Oct 4 to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan.
“We have started meeting with the representatives of political parties so that the date and venue for the moot is finalised,” he said, adding that since the PPP had taken a clear stance over the creation of new provinces, the opposition had decided to invite it as well.
In the recent past, the proposal for the creation of new administrative units was first floated by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi in July. The proposition drew strong reactions from government ministers, while the country’s leading lawyers’ bodies adopted divergent positions.
The PPP, which rules Sindh, has strongly opposed any division of the province and maintains that any decision to create new provinces must be taken through the constitutional and parliamentary process and with political consensus.
Meanwhile, the relationship between the PPP and the PML-N had also been strained lately during acrimonious election campaigns in Azad Jammu and Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan.
The TTAP also plans invite other parties to the opposition’s moot.
Yousafzai said Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam (JUI), Awami National Party (ANP) and Jamaat-i-Islami would also be invited to the moot, but the ruling PML-N and its ally in the Centre, Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan, would not be extended an invitation.
The TTAP has also formed a six-member committee to hold consultations with political parties and reach an agreement on the agenda for the proposed MPC.

deduped_items.title: Shein shares dive more than 11% after earnings disappoint
deduped_items.summary: Shares in Chinese fast-fashion giant Shein plunged more than 11 percent in Hong Kong on Tuesday after releasing disappointing financial results. The company has faced scrutiny over its environmental footprint and allegations of human rights violations, and faces growing competition from low-cost e-commerce companies such as Temu and AliExpress. The firm said on Monday that […]
deduped_items.body_text:
Shares in Chinese fast-fashion giant Shein plunged more than 11 percent in Hong Kong on Tuesday after releasing disappointing financial results.
The company has faced scrutiny over its environmental footprint and allegations of human rights violations, and faces growing competition from low-cost e-commerce companies such as Temu and AliExpress.
The firm said on Monday that revenue grew just one percent on-year in the first six months of the year, while its operating profit halved.
By around lunch on Tuesday, Shein’s share price had pared some of the losses but was still down 10.9 percent at HK$31.44.
Monday’s results were Shein’s first since its high-profile initial public offering this month, which put the company’s valuation at around $26.3 billion — well short of the nearly $100 billion during private fundraising rounds in 2022.
Net revenue from Europe fell 13.9 percent to nearly $3.8 billion for the second quarter, Shein reported.
The decrease “reflects a decline in sales volume as we raised prices and lowered online advertising spending” in anticipation of the removal of the customs duty exemption, the company said.
Another key market, the United States, saw revenue drop six percent in April-June, reflecting the impact of tariffs.
Since its first day of trading on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in September, Shein’s share price has fallen more than 35 percent.
The accelerating decline in Shein’s operating profit “clouds the extent of a 2027 recovery from freight relief and an unproven push into higher-priced brands”, said Catherine Lim, an analyst at Business Intelligence.

Shares in Chinese fast-fashion giant Shein plunged more than 11 percent in Hong Kong on Tuesday after releasing disappointing financial results.
The company has faced scrutiny over its environmental footprint and allegations of human rights violations, and faces growing competition from low-cost e-commerce companies such as Temu and AliExpress.
The firm said on Monday that revenue grew just one percent on-year in the first six months of the year, while its operating profit halved.
By around lunch on Tuesday, Shein’s share price had pared some of the losses but was still down 10.9 percent at HK$31.44.
Monday’s results were Shein’s first since its high-profile initial public offering this month, which put the company’s valuation at around $26.3 billion — well short of the nearly $100 billion during private fundraising rounds in 2022.
Net revenue from Europe fell 13.9 percent to nearly $3.8 billion for the second quarter, Shein reported.
The decrease “reflects a decline in sales volume as we raised prices and lowered online advertising spending” in anticipation of the removal of the customs duty exemption, the company said.
Another key market, the United States, saw revenue drop six percent in April-June, reflecting the impact of tariffs.
Since its first day of trading on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in September, Shein’s share price has fallen more than 35 percent.
The accelerating decline in Shein’s operating profit “clouds the extent of a 2027 recovery from freight relief and an unproven push into higher-priced brands”, said Catherine Lim, an analyst at Business Intelligence.
“Management plans to absorb freight and tariff costs rather than raise prices to protect the company’s competitive position,” she said, adding that localising stock in Europe will lead to higher logistics costs in the short term.

deduped_items.summary: Shares in Chinese fast-fashion giant Shein plunged more than 11 percent in Hong Kong on Tuesday after releasing disappointing financial results. deduped_items.body_text:
Shares in Chinese fast-fashion giant Shein plunged more than 11 percent in Hong Kong on Tuesday after releasing disappointing financial results.
The company has faced scrutiny over its environmental footprint and allegations of human rights violations, and faces growing competition from low-cost e-commerce companies such as Temu and AliExpress.
The firm said on Monday that revenue grew just one percent on-year in the first six months of the year, while its operating profit halved.
By around lunch on Tuesday, Shein’s share price had pared some of the losses but was still down 10.9 percent at HK$31.44.
Monday’s results were Shein’s first since its high-profile initial public offering this month, which put the company’s valuation at around $26.3 billion — well short of the nearly $100 billion during private fundraising rounds in 2022.
Net revenue from Europe fell 13.9 percent to nearly $3.8 billion for the second quarter, Shein reported.
The decrease “reflects a decline in sales volume as we raised prices and lowered online advertising spending” in anticipation of the removal of the customs duty exemption, the company said.
Another key market, the United States, saw revenue drop six percent in April-June, reflecting the impact of tariffs.
Since its first day of trading on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in September, Shein’s share price has fallen more than 35 percent.
The accelerating decline in Shein’s operating profit “clouds the extent of a 2027 recovery from freight relief and an unproven push into higher-priced brands”, said Catherine Lim, an analyst at Business Intelligence.
“Management plans to absorb freight and tariff costs rather than raise prices to protect the company’s competitive position,” she said, adding that localising stock in Europe will lead to higher logistics costs in the short term.

deduped_items.summary: Shares in Chinese fast-fashion giant Shein plunged more than 11 percent in Hong Kong on Tuesday after releasing disappointing financial results. The company has faced scrutiny over its environmental footprint and allegations of human rights violations, and faces growing competition from low-cost e-commerce companies such as Temu and AliExpress. The firm said on Monday that […]
deduped_items.body_text:
Shares in Chinese fast-fashion giant Shein plunged more than 11 percent in Hong Kong on Tuesday after releasing disappointing financial results.
The company has faced scrutiny over its environmental footprint and allegations of human rights violations, and faces growing competition from low-cost e-commerce companies such as Temu and AliExpress.
The firm said on Monday that revenue grew just one percent on-year in the first six months of the year, while its operating profit halved.
By around lunch on Tuesday, Shein’s share price had pared some of the losses but was still down 10.9 percent at HK$31.44.
Monday’s results were Shein’s first since its high-profile initial public offering this month, which put the company’s valuation at around $26.3 billion — well short of the nearly $100 billion during private fundraising rounds in 2022.
Net revenue from Europe fell 13.9 percent to nearly $3.8 billion for the second quarter, Shein reported.
The decrease “reflects a decline in sales volume as we raised prices and lowered online advertising spending” in anticipation of the removal of the customs duty exemption, the company said.
Another key market, the United States, saw revenue drop six percent in April-June, reflecting the impact of tariffs.
Since its first day of trading on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in September, Shein’s share price has fallen more than 35 percent.
The accelerating decline in Shein’s operating profit “clouds the extent of a 2027 recovery from freight relief and an unproven push into higher-priced brands”, said Catherine Lim, an analyst at Business Intelligence.
“Management plans to absorb freight and tariff costs rather than raise prices to protect the company’s competitive position,” she said, adding that localising stock in Europe will lead to higher logistics costs in the short term.

In an update on the case, which has drawn public attention, the force said the number of reports had risen to 1,503 as of Tuesday, from about 1,200 two weeks earlier. It added that all the transactions had been cancelled. Speaking at a Kowloon City district council meeting, Commissioner of Police Joe Chow...
deduped_items.body_text:
Hong Kong police record 1,503 suspicious iPhone charges so far worth HK$30m
Police say all unauthorised iPhone 18 Pro transactions have been cancelled and Apple has been asked to review its payment security measures
Hong Kong police have received more than 1,500 reports of suspicious credit card transactions involving Apple’s new iPhone 18 Pro series, totalling more than HK$30 million (US$3.82 million).
In an update on the case, which has drawn public attention, the force said the number of reports had risen to 1,503 as of Tuesday, from about 1,200 two weeks earlier. It added that all the transactions had been cancelled.
Speaking at a Kowloon City district council meeting, Commissioner of Police Joe Chow Yat-ming noted that in the cases involved, Apple’s online commerce security measures were not in effect and the transactions did not require verification.
“This meant that one-time passwords or mobile app verification were not required, allowing fraudsters to place large orders using illegally obtained credit card information,” he said.

Hong Kong police have received more than 1,500 reports of suspicious credit card transactions involving Apple’s new iPhone 18 Pro series, totalling more than HK$30 million (US$3.82 million).
In an update on the case, which has drawn public attention, the force said the number of reports had risen to 1,503 as of Tuesday, from about 1,200 two weeks earlier. It added that all the transactions had been cancelled.
Speaking at a Kowloon City district council meeting, Commissioner of Police Joe Chow Yat-ming noted that in the cases involved, Apple’s online commerce security measures were not in effect and the transactions did not require verification.
“This meant that one-time passwords or mobile app verification were not required, allowing fraudsters to place large orders using illegally obtained credit card information,” he said.

Since the September 2026 rollout, however, unstable networks and incompatible devices have caused widespread confusion. A source in the province told Daily NK […]

deduped_items.summary: China is set to cut tariffs on a broad range of U.S. agricultural goods, from corn and wheat to meat and dairy, but top import item soybeans were excluded from a tariff-reduction list its commerce ministry issued on Monday. Reuters Chief China Commodities Correspondent Lewis Jackson takes a look at what we know about Donald Trump's proposed U.S.-China Board of Trade.

deduped_items.title: U.S. prosecutors reopen alleged Cornell University gang rape case after accuser files lawsuit
deduped_items.summary: Victim alleges she was drugged and assaulted by seven members of a fraternity in 2024 and that some of the men involved were allowed to write essays to mitigate their conduct
deduped_items.body_text:
U.S. prosecutors reopen alleged Cornell University gang rape case after accuser files lawsuit
Victim alleges she was drugged and assaulted by seven members of a fraternity in 2024 and that some of the men involved were allowed to write essays to mitigate their conduct
U.S. prosecutors reopened an investigation Monday into an alleged gang rape at Cornell University following claims the elite college failed to properly punish the men involved.
The alleged victim said in a civil lawsuit this month she was drugged with ketamine, assaulted and raped in 2024 by seven members of the Chi Phi fraternity, a social club for male students.
Cornell closed the fraternity and temporarily suspended the students involved, several of whom were later expelled.
The newly released details of the alleged incident have fuelled allegations that the university was too lenient and reignited a debate over sexual assault on U.S. campuses.
Matthew Van Houten, district attorney for Tompkins County in New York, said that he plans to file criminal charges against the seven men.
He said his office chose in 2024 not to prosecute because the victim’s testimony did not establish a lack of consent, but had now decided to do so in light of her latest allegations.
“I recognize the reality that it can take years of therapy and healing for victims of sexual assaults to fully process and understand what happened to them,” Van Houten said in a statement.
“Seeking justice sometimes requires us to reconsider or reopen cases when we are provided with additional evidence.”
Kyle Kimball, vice president of university relations at Cornell, said the Ivy League school supports the decision to reinvestigate the case.
He also rejected a claim, made in the civil lawsuit, that the suspects were offered the opportunity to write essays to mitigate their conduct.
“Any suggestion that the university did not impose consequential punishments for those involved is false,” Kimball said.
The 101-page civil lawsuit filed in New York gives graphic details on the alleged assault of the woman, whose identity is being protected.
Notably, it provides a screenshot of a Snapchat group message advertising “free pussy” during the incident, apparently an invitation for other fraternity members to take part.
The suit seeks financial damages from Cornell and the seven suspects, adding that the woman has suffered “severe emotional and psychological distress.”
British actor Florence Pugh has voiced her anger about the case, saying she felt “uneasy and sick and anxious” after hearing about it.
“Colleges/schools/universities repeatedly fail women around the world,” she wrote on Instagram.
“You build men that get taught through time and time again that they can do extreme harm and that they won’t be harmed in return,” Pugh said.
Prominent Democratic lawmaker Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez condemned a “culture of rape” at elite institutions like Cornell.
“Jane Doe, that survivor, lost her education because you can’t stay in school when something like that happens to you,” Ocasio-Cortez said Sunday.
“She had to lose her education, and those men were protected by an institution and granted an Ivy League degree as a reward. Never again.”
